faq.q: What is there to do in Colonia del Sacramento's Barrio Histórico?
faq.a: You can cover Colonia's UNESCO Barrio Histórico on foot in about 4–5 hours including lunch: walk the ~12-block grid, the 1700s-era Calle de los Suspiros, the Plaza Mayor house-museums, and the Portón de Campo drawbridge gate, then climb the 111-step lighthouse for river-and-town views. It is compact because the Portuguese laid it out in 1680.

faq.q: Is Colonia worth an overnight, or just a day trip?
faq.a: Worth the overnight — that is the town's quiet secret. Most travelers arrive on the day-ferry from Buenos Aires, so staying a night gives you the emptied cobbles at dusk and dawn and a sunset on the Rambla as the Río de la Plata turns copper. Book ahead: the top boutique, Charco, has only 8 rooms.

faq.q: Can you do a wine day from Colonia del Sacramento?
faq.a: Yes — the wine day runs ~80 km up-river to Carmelo, Uruguay's Tannat sub-region, with estate lunches at Narbona (a 1909-founded estate) and Bodega Cordano. Book it guided or with a driver: the fire to plan around is drink-and-drive on rural roads.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Colonia?
faq.a: Footing, not crime. The single most common visitor injury is a twist or fall on the Barrio Histórico's uneven 300-year-old cobbles, which turn slick in the wet. Wear closed, gripped footwear and take extra care in rain and after dark — unguided walking is otherwise fine. Tap water is potable, and 911 is the nationwide emergency line.

faq.q: Do I need my passport for the Buenos Aires day-ferry?
faq.a: Yes — the crossing is an Argentina→Uruguay international border, and it is the single most common trip-planning error. Passengers clear immigration and customs at the terminal before boarding and check-in closes early, so arrive 1.5–2 hours before departure with your passport for both legs.

faq.q: Can I book Costalegre through TravelWell right now?
faq.a: No — it is content-only. Jalisco sits at US State Dept Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" (May 29, 2026), and the advisory's four named no-restriction carve-outs (Guadalajara Metro, Puerto Vallarta, Chapala, Ajijic) do not include the southern-Jalisco Costalegre coast, so book_enabled=FALSE.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on Costalegre?
faq.a: The road transfer, and the remoteness. Ground access runs through non-carve-out southern Jalisco on Highway 200 and secondary roads, and the advisory warns against secondary highways after dark — the hold reason. The coast is remote: serious cases route ~1.5 hr to Manzanillo or 2–4 hr to Puerto Vallarta, so air-evac insurance is essential.

faq.q: What makes Costalegre a true ultra coast?
faq.a: Three private enclaves with their own airstrips. Careyes (clifftop castles + ~50 staffed villas), Cuixmala (a ~25,000-acre Goldsmith biosphere estate) and Las Alamandas (an 18-suite gated boutique) form one of Mexico's most private ultra nodes — the private-air arrival is the crux of a possible future clean-pass.

faq.q: What are the best beaches and islands here?
faq.a: Chamela Bay and Tenacatita. Chamela is dotted with marine-reserve islets (Isla Cocinas, Isla Pajarera) reachable by panga, and Tenacatita (~30 min north of Barra de Navidad) is famed for clear, calm water for snorkel, kayak and SUP — the calmest bays on a ~200-mile coast.

faq.q: When can I see whales on Costalegre?
faq.a: December to March. Humpbacks migrate and breach offshore along the whole coast in the dry winter season — the same window as peak ultra-villa demand — while the Chamela–Cuixmala biosphere adds turtle nesting and dry-forest wildlife. Keep a regulated distance on any boat tour.

85% of ski area above 1,800 m + 2,100+ snow cannons; 6-day 3 Vallees pass EUR 409 (2025/26)
Courchevel Altiport at 2,008 m — world's first mountain airfield (opened 1961/62), 537 m runway at 18.6% gradient, no go-around
Most Michelin-starred ski resort on earth: 7 starred restaurants, 13 stars; Le 1947 a Cheval Blanc holds 3 stars
Five Palace-distinction hotels (Atout France label, 2010; 31 in France): Cheval Blanc, Les Airelles, L'Apogee, Le K2 Palace, Barriere Les Neiges
France's first purpose-built ski resort (founded 1946); 80th anniversary in 2026; Emile Allais + first Sno-Cat grooming 1959
Aquamotion 10,500 m2 — largest aquatic centre in the French Alps, only in-resort indoor surf wave in Europe
Men's Alpine Ski World Cup 13-15 Mar 2026 on L'Eclipse; confirmed 2030 French-Alps Olympics speed venue + ski jumping at Le Praz
International Pyrotechnic Art Festival (Feb-early Mar); Moriond Racing 3 km toboggan run through 8 tunnels

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Courchevel?
faq.a: The mountain, not crime - avalanche off-piste. Courchevel is high alpine terrain (Saulire 2,738 m); check the Meteo-France BERA avalanche bulletin daily (5-level scale, Haute-Tarentaise massif), never ski off-piste without a transceiver, shovel, probe and a qualified guide, and treat closed pistes as closed. Mountain rescue is 112.

faq.q: 1850 or 1650 (Moriond) - which Courchevel village should I stay in?
faq.a: Courchevel 1850 is the glamour address - best ski access, luxury shopping, palace hotels and the jet-set scene; Moriond (1650) is more traditional, sunnier (a south-facing sun-trap), better value with a younger apres crowd; Le Praz (1300) is the quiet, characterful base.

faq.q: Do I have to be a millionaire to ski Courchevel?
faq.a: No - 1850 is genuinely jet-set (palace suites ~EUR2,000-8,000+/night), but you can ski the same 600 km of Les 3 Vallees staying in Moriond, Le Praz or nearby La Tania for a fraction of that. The lift pass and slopes are the same; only the bed and bar bill change. (Nightly rates are seasonal - verify before travel.)

faq.q: When is the best time to ski Courchevel?
faq.a: December-April, with March the sweet spot - reliable high-altitude snow, longer daylight and lighter crowds; January brings the coldest, most reliable cover; late December and February half-terms are busiest and priciest. (Season dates and crowd/price patterns vary by year - verify before travel.)

faq.q: Is there true ski-in/ski-out luxury in Courchevel?
faq.a: Yes - it's built for it: Le Strato, Courcheneige and premium catered chalets put you on the snow, and 1850's five Palace-distinction hotels are steps from the lifts.

faq.q: Is Courchevel good for beginners and families?
faq.a: Very - it's one of the best places in the Alps to learn: each village has its own nursery slopes, and the wide gentle green runs above 1850 plus Moriond's magic-carpet progression zones and Family Park make it family-gold.

name: Courmayeur
line: The Italian side of Mont Blanc

key_facts: Courmayeur at 1,224 m on the Italian side of Monte Bianco (Mont Blanc), Aosta Valley; spa resort since the 18th c; alpinism from the 19th c
Skyway Monte Bianco (opened 2015, ~EUR 138M — world's most expensive cable car): Pontal d'Entreves 1,300 m -> Pavillon du Mont-Frety 2,173 m -> Punta Helbronner 3,466 m, rotating 80-person cabins
Ski area Courmayeur-Checrouit/Val Veny: 41.5 km pistes (16 easy/21.5 int/4 diff), 1,205-2,755 m, 18 lifts, ~1,550 m vertical; season ~28 Nov 2026-4 Apr 2027
Toula Glacier + Vallee Blanche off-piste from Punta Helbronner (guided-only); Courmayeur alpine-guide society founded 1850 (2nd in the world)
Pre-Saint-Didier QC Terme thermal baths: 40+ experiences, outdoor pools with Mont Blanc views, entry from ~EUR 46; adults 14+
Skyway return fares 2026: Punta Helbronner adult ~EUR 59-63; Pavillon ~EUR 25-27; SkyVertigo walkway + 360 observatory + ~900-species botanical garden + Torino Hut link
Monte Bianco Ski & Snowboard School (founded 1936, Italy's largest) turns 90 in 2026; Mont Blanc Tunnel to Chamonix opened 16 Jul 1965
Summer trail calendar: Gran Trail Courmayeur (GTC30/55/100, 10-12 Jul 2026) + UTMB (from 28 Aug 2026, ~174 km, ~9,900 m climb); Courmayeur Design Week + Italia Polo Challenge

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Cozumel?
faq.a: Decompression discipline, not crime — this is a repetitive multi-day dive island. Follow DAN's no-fly windows strictly (12h single, 18h multi-day, 24h conservative), because Cozumel's day-boat profiles stack dives fast; the island has multiple chambers, but a bad no-fly call is the classic mistake. Also plan for dengue (repellent), bottled water and hurricane season (Jun–Nov).

faq.q: Is drift diving in Cozumel dangerous?
faq.a: No, when you take the drift briefing seriously — but it is not passive. Expect a near-constant ~1.5-knot current that does the swimming for you; do a controlled descent, stay with the group and dive master, deploy an SMB, and dive within your certification. Santa Rosa Wall is expert-only; Palancar Gardens suits most certified divers.

faq.q: What are the best dive sites in Cozumel, and can beginners dive them?
faq.a: Palancar Gardens is the everyone-friendly classic — coral pinnacles, archways and swim-throughs at 100-ft-plus visibility with mild current — while Santa Rosa Wall and Columbia Deep are advanced drifts. Beginners and newly certified divers do best at Palancar; Santa Rosa, dropping from ~15 m into the blue, is expert-only.

faq.q: Can I do a liveaboard from Cozumel?
faq.a: Not from Cozumel itself — it is a day-boat island. True liveaboard-style multi-day diving goes to Banco Chinchorro, ~30–35 nm off Costa Maya, launched from Xcalak or Mahahual to the south, not Cozumel. The luxury alternative near Cozumel is a private crewed dive-yacht charter, since overnight liveaboards are effectively banned inside the national park.

faq.q: Can non-divers snorkel Cozumel, and what's the reef fee?
faq.a: Yes — the reef is superb for snorkelers, from Palancar shallows to the El Cielo starfish sandbar by catamaran. Everyone entering the marine park pays the reef bracelet, MX$220 (~US$13) per person per day as of Jan 2026; snorkel tours carry no no-fly restriction, making them a good last-day option before a flight.

faq.q: Is Cozumel good for a honeymoon or a couples' dive trip?
faq.a: Yes — it pairs world-class diving with real staffed villas. Luxury Cozumel and Villa Experience run oceanfront staffed homes (chef, concierge) from ~US$450/night, and there is no branded ultra flag on-island, so for hotel-brand luxury couples ferry to Mayakoba (Rosewood, Banyan Tree) ~an hour away.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Cozumel?
faq.a: December–March is peak, with the calmest seas, clearest skies and legendary 200-ft-plus visibility. November and May are the value sweet spots — near-peak conditions at ~25–40% (Nov) and ~20–30% (May) below Dec rates; May–September brings the warmest, calmest water (~27–28°C) but summer humidity and hurricane risk.

faq.q: What makes Cuenca a UNESCO World Heritage city?
faq.a: Its historic center is a living colonial grid crowned by the New Cathedral — the Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepción, whose three blue-and-white domes were tiled with glaze from old Czechoslovakia and whose towers were left truncated by a load-bearing miscalculation. Built from 1885 over nearly a century, it is free to enter, with dome access monetized.

faq.q: Is Ingapirca worth the day trip from Cuenca?
faq.a: Yes — it is Ecuador's largest Inca ruin, ~80 km north (~3,150 m), a rare Inca-Cañari blend crowned by the elliptical Temple of the Sun, the only one of its kind in the empire, built atop a Cañari sacred rock. Go guided full-day (highest margin) or self-serve by Transportes Cañar bus (~$3.50).

faq.q: Is Cuenca a good romantic honeymoon base?
faq.a: Yes — it is a gentle, walkable heritage-city honeymoon, not a beach one. Restored 19th-century casonas like Mansión Alcázar (three blocks from Parque Calderón, with garden, spa and fine dining) and Hotel Santa Lucía anchor the boutique-colonial base, with the Baños de Cuenca thermal circuit — water surfacing at ~75°C — 20 minutes out.

faq.q: Can you hike El Cajas from Cuenca on your own?
faq.a: Only partly — go guided beyond the marked loops. El Cajas (28,000 ha, 786 lakes) has no cell signal and weather that turns in minutes; only the Laguna Toreadora and Laguna Llaviucu loops are well marked, and exposure deaths have occurred on unmarked trails. The ~2-hour Toreadora loop (~3,960 m) is self-guided-feasible for the acclimatized.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Cuenca?
faq.a: Altitude, not crime. Cuenca sits at ~2,560 m, just above the 2,500 m AMS threshold — effects are usually mild and pass in 2–3 days — but El Cajas hiking at ~3,960–4,000 m is genuine high-altitude exertion. Take a slow first day, hydrate 3+ L/day, skip alcohol early, and do Cajas after a day or two in the city rather than on arrival.

faq.q: Is El Cajas dangerous?
faq.a: It can be if you go off-trail unprepared — exposure deaths have occurred there. The park has no cell signal and weather changes in minutes; only the Toreadora and Llaviucu loops are well marked. Guided is strongly preferred beyond those two loops; carry layers, a rain shell, water and food regardless of forecast, and hike after acclimatizing.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Curacao?
faq.a: Dive discipline, not danger. Hold the no-fly 18-24h window and manage deep profiles (the Superior Producer sits at 30m). Reassuringly, Curacao Medical Center has an on-island recompression chamber - the ABC's regional dive-emergency facility.

faq.q: Is Curacao a liveaboard destination?
faq.a: No - like its ABC neighbours it is shore + day-boat diving only (packages, private charters, PADI 5-star operators), not a liveaboard base. Book it as a resort-and-boat dive trip, not a Dive Liveaboards sailing.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit and dive Curacao?
faq.a: Year-round - Curacao is south of the hurricane belt with warm, clear water all year. December-April is the drier peak; May-November is warmer and quieter (best value), with the odd short shower.

faq.q: Which Curacao dive sites should I not miss?
faq.a: The Tugboat (5m, beginner-perfect), the Mushroom Forest + Blue Room boat run, the Superior Producer deep wreck (30m), and a Klein Curacao islet day; many west-end sites are also shore-accessible.

faq.q: Is there more to Curacao than diving?
faq.a: Yes - it's the ABC's cultural anchor: UNESCO Willemstad (Handelskade, floating market, Queen Emma pontoon bridge), the island's Jewish and slavery heritage, and Mt Christoffel to hike - a rounded island, not a single-note dive stop.

faq.q: Do you need to acclimatize before Rainbow Mountain?
faq.a: Yes — acclimatize 1–2 days minimum in Cusco or the valley before any high hike, and never climb Rainbow Mountain on your first or second day. It matters because more than a third of travelers to Cusco feel altitude sickness, the summit sits at ~5,200 m (roughly 11% effective oxygen), and the core risk is acute mountain sickness, not terrain. Go guided — reputable operators carry oxygen, manage pace and pull travelers who deteriorate.

faq.q: What does the Cusco Tourist Ticket cover?
faq.a: The integral Boleto Turístico costs S/130 (~$35), is valid 10 days across 16 sites, and is cash-only in soles with no online option. Note what it does not cover: Machu Picchu, Qorikancha, the Cathedral, Rainbow Mountain and Humantay all require separate admission, so budget those as pass-through costs on top.

faq.q: Which are the best luxury lodges in the Sacred Valley and Cusco?
faq.a: The honeymoon spine runs from Cusco's Belmond Palacio Nazarenas (55 oxygen-enriched all-suites) and Belmond Monasterio (a 16th-century monastery, 117 rooms) out to the valley's explora Valle Sagrado, Sol y Luna (Relais & Châteaux) and Tambo del Inka — the Luxury Collection resort with its own private rail station to Machu Picchu.

faq.q: When do you need to book for Inti Raymi and peak season?
faq.a: Book 3–4 months out — by late March, ideally February — for June–August and Inti Raymi trips, because capacity, not price, is what runs out. Inti Raymi (the Festival of the Sun) falls on June 24 and sells the city out months ahead, and Machu Picchu tickets, trains and hotels are capacity-capped in peak season.

faq.q: What's the real risk in Cusco — is it altitude?
faq.a: Yes — altitude outranks crime by a wide margin. Cusco sits at ~3,400 m and Rainbow Mountain at ~5,200 m, and more than a third of travelers feel altitude sickness (soroche), some moderate-to-severe. Acclimatize 1–2 days before any high hike, ascend gradually, hydrate, use coca, and discuss prophylactic acetazolamide (Diamox) with a physician; the emergency number is 105.

faq.q: Is Rainbow Mountain dangerous?
faq.a: The danger is altitude, not the walk. At ~5,200 m the core risk is acute mountain sickness, so guided is strongly preferred — reputable operators carry oxygen, manage pace and pull travelers who deteriorate — and the non-negotiable rule is to acclimatize 1–2 days first. Travelers who want the color without the 5,200 m gut-check can take Palccoyo, the gentler-altitude "rainbow" alternative.

Caps the number of lift tickets sold daily - lower-volume BY DESIGN, 'typically reaches capacity' at holidays; the luxury/spend leader (ski valets, mountain hosts, on-mountain fine dining)

'EXPANDED EXCELLENCE' Mayflower/East Village integration = largest resort expansion in ski history; 'more than doubled' since Dec 2024 (11 new lifts, ~100 new runs, new East Village base LIVE); ~4,300 skiable acres now / 4,500-acre TARGET 2026-27 - do NOT hard-state ~5,700
On-mountain FINE DINING is a signature (Cast & Cut seafood, Fireside Dining, Royal Street Cafe - reservations required)
Ultra lodging: Stein Eriksen Lodge (Utah's longest-running Forbes Five-Star) + St. Regis Deer Valley (private funicular) + Montage + Goldener Hirsch + Grand Summit
US-TRAFFIC CANDOR: spend leader, lower-volume by design (ticket cap); no per-resort count published - consensus only

SLC ~36 mi / ~40 min via I-80/Parley's; Sundance 22 Jan-1 Feb 2026 = final Utah edition (Park City host, NOT a Deer Valley venue); 2002 Olympic freestyle heritage + expected 2034 moguls; Deer Valley Music Festival (summer)

faq.q: What is Djerba known for?
faq.a: A Mediterranean island of beaches and thalassotherapy spas, the UNESCO island landscape of whitewashed villages, and El Ghriba - one of the oldest synagogues on Earth. A soft-adventure counterpoint to the medina and the Sahara.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Djerba?
faq.a: April-June and September-October - warm sea and fewer crowds. July-August is peak European beach season; December-February is mild, quiet and cheapest.

faq.q: Can I combine Djerba with the rest of Tunisia?
faq.a: Yes - it's the beach-and-wellness leg. Pair it with Tunis and Carthage (culture) and the Sahara oases (Tozeur/Douz) for the whole country in one loop.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in the Douro?
faq.a: Not crime — sun, water and the road: the terraces are steep and sun-exposed, the Douro is a dammed locked working river (follow crew on boats), and the N222 valley road is a tight switchback — use a driver or the Porto-Pinhao train, and never drive after tastings.

faq.q: When is the best time for a Douro cruise?
faq.a: Spring to autumn (roughly March-November), with September-October the harvest peak — you cruise past picking in progress and the quintas are liveliest, so harvest sailings book earliest.

faq.q: Which cruise lines sail the Douro from Porto?
faq.a: Seven confirmed — Viking, AmaWaterways, Avalon, CroisiEurope, Scenic, Emerald and Uniworld — because Porto is the single embarkation gateway for the ~8-day run up to Regua, Pinhao and the Spanish border.

faq.q: What's the difference between Port and Douro wine?
faq.a: Both come from the same Alto Douro terraces, but Port is fortified and aged in the Vila Nova de Gaia lodges (an 18th-century tradition), while Douro DOC is unfortified table wine — taste both, one at a Gaia lodge, one at a valley quinta.

faq.q: Where should I stay for a luxury Douro base?
faq.a: Two anchors: Six Senses Douro Valley, a restored 19th-century manor with a vineyard-heritage spa, for the valley itself; or The Yeatman above the Gaia Port lodges — 109 terraced river-view rooms, a two-Michelin-star table and a Caudalie Vinotherapie spa.

faq.q: Is the Douro good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — a quiet, high-romance wine landscape: a river-view quinta suite, a private terrace over the vines at sunset, and a Michelin dinner across from Porto's lit Ribeira. It reads couples, not crowds.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for Dubai, and can I book it through TravelWell?
faq.a: The UAE is at U.S. State Department Level 3 - Reconsider Travel, and you cannot book Dubai through TravelWell right now. An armed conflict that began 28 February 2026 - U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, then Iranian retaliatory missile and drone strikes across all six GCC states, with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed to commercial shipping and a State 'depart now' order on 2 March 2026 - is ongoing as of 2026-08-10. TravelWell books Level 3 destinations only through a consent gate, and that gate is not built, so no Gulf destination is bookable today regardless of level. This is fast-moving: re-verify the level and the flight picture before any travel.
faq.source: level+conflict supplied by Strategy Claude from a 2026-08-09 read of the US Embassy UAE alert 4 Jun 2026 + State-advisory press; conflict corroborated 2026-08-10 via F1/FIA cancellation coverage (Sky Sports/PlanetF1 via web search)

faq.q: How are flights and airspace affected?
faq.a: Airports are open but subject to short-notice closures, and there have been renewed UAE airspace restrictions (reported 4-11 May 2026). As a concrete example, American Airlines cancelled its Philadelphia-Doha route through the end of 2026, with a restart targeted for January 2027. Build slack into any itinerary and confirm every segment close to departure.
faq.source: supplied by Strategy Claude from a 2026-08-09 read

faq.q: What would a Dubai trip cover once it is bookable again?
faq.a: The core is Downtown (Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall, the Fountain), the Museum of the Future, old Dubai at Al Fahidi with a Dubai Creek abra crossing and the Gold Souk, the Jumeirah beach strip past the Burj Al Arab, Palm Jumeirah, and a desert dune-safari evening. The Dubai Shopping Festival (Jan-Feb) is the marquee event window.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Dubai?
faq.a: November-March is the cool, dry season and the event peak (including the Shopping Festival); summer (Jun-Sep) is very hot, routinely above 40C. This is planning-only guidance while the destination is held content-only.

faq.q: Is there anything specific to know about safety in the city itself?
faq.a: Beyond the regional conflict and the airspace risk, Dubai's own street-crime level is low; the binding constraints right now are the Level 3 advisory, the flight-disruption risk, and the fact that the destination is held content-only. Re-verify the advisory before acting on anything here.
faq.source: levels supplied by Strategy Claude from a 2026-08-09 read; en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Dubai (accessed 2026-08-10)

faq.q: Is the East Cape a good honeymoon base?
faq.a: Yes — it holds two of Mexico's most serious luxury resorts on one estate. Costa Palmas fronts a rare swimmable Cabo-side beach (3 km) with the Four Seasons and Amanvari, 45 minutes from SJD, so couples get calm water plus branded ultra away from the corridor crowds.

faq.q: When can I see whales in the Sea of Cortez here?
faq.a: Late December to early April, with the blue-whale peak Feb–Apr. Gray, humpback, blue and fin whales all pass offshore, on day tours or private charters out of the East Cape — one of Earth's richest whale seas.

faq.q: When is the fishing and the wind best on the East Cape?
faq.a: Two opposite seasons: billfish and dorado peak May to early November in glass-calm water, while the El Norte wind turns Los Barriles into a 15–25 kt kite and windsurf arena Dec–March. Pick the season for the sport you came for.

faq.q: Can you walk on the Perito Moreno glacier?
faq.a: Yes, but only with a certified guide. "Mini-trekking" straps you into crampons for ~1.5 hours on the ice (a ~10-hour day with boat and transfer), and "Big Ice" gives ~3.5 hours deep among crevasses and ice caves (ages ~18–50, high difficulty). Ice-trekking is guided-only — crevasses and moulins are lethal — and Big Ice runs mid-September to end of April.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit El Calafate and Patagonia?
faq.a: Austral summer — December through February, with January the busiest — is peak, with longest daylight (up to ~17 hours) and 8–17 °C. Best conditions run Oct–Mar, and October and March give the best weather-to-crowds ratio; peak lodges and treks sell out 6–12 months ahead, so book early.

faq.q: Which honeymoon lodge should we book in Patagonia?
faq.a: EOLO – Patagonia's Spirit is the flagship: a 17-room Relais & Châteaux full-board lodge on a 4,000-ha estate on the Perito Moreno road, sold via the Virtuoso/Fora advisor lane. It sells out 6–12 months ahead for peak summer, so fire early — the "Perito Moreno at sunrise, fire-warmed lodge, no cell signal" pitch writes itself.

faq.q: Where do Antarctica cruises leave from?
faq.a: Ushuaia — the Southern Hemisphere's Antarctica embarkation port, and the last town before the Drake Passage. Every peninsula voyage that matters departs Nov–Mar, with entry expedition fares ~US$12,000–15,000+ per person (luxury far higher) on Ponant, Silversea, Lindblad and Aurora; the best cabins go 12+ months out.

faq.q: Can you ski near El Calafate?
faq.a: Not at El Calafate itself, but Bariloche flips to ski season while El Calafate quiets in winter. Cerro Catedral — the largest ski resort in South America, with 70+ pistes — runs Jun–Sep, with the best snow Aug–early September. This is the region's counter-season revenue lane.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Patagonia?
faq.a: Wind and weather. Patagonian wind and rapid weather change are the number-one hazard — gusts funnel through the Fitz Roy cirque at 80–100 km/h even on "calm" days, and wind chill at the lagoon can push effective temps below freezing. El Calafate, El Chaltén and Ushuaia are remote, so serious trauma routes to Buenos Aires by air; build buffer days and carry insurance covering repatriation and evacuation.

faq.q: Is glacier ice-trekking dangerous?
faq.a: It is a hard rule, not a preference: guided-only. Both mini-trekking (~1.5 hr) and Big Ice (~3.5 hr, crevasses and ice caves, ages ~18–50) require crampons and a certified glacier guide, because crevasses and moulins are lethal — ice-trekking should never be presented as self-guided under any circumstance.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Drink-and-drive on wine roads, and the cold Pacific — not the Mexicali cartel context, which lies far east and is never transited on the Ensenada corridor. Use a driver for any Valle de Guadalupe tasting day, treat the open Pacific as look-don't-swim (strong riptides, cold water), and route serious trauma north to San Diego.

faq.q: Where do I eat the famous fish tacos?
faq.a: Around the Mercado Negro, where they were arguably invented. Ensenada is credited as the birthplace of the modern Baja fish taco (c.1960), and doña Sabina Bandera's La Guerrerense cart — a 2013 World Street Food Congress medalist and MICHELIN-recognized name — is the must-eat; nearby San Quintín Kumamoto oysters extend the culinary lane.

faq.q: What is La Bufadora and when's it best?
faq.a: It's one of North America's largest marine geysers, best at high tide. On the Punta Banda peninsula, La Bufadora shoots seawater up to ~100 feet when swell compresses air in a sea cave; entry is free (nominal parking), and winter swells give the biggest spouts. Mind the slippery, unfenced cliff edges.

faq.q: Can I do Valle de Guadalupe as a day trip?
faq.a: Yes — it's ~40 minutes northeast, with 250+ wineries and a farm-to-table scene. Book a guided wine day with a driver rather than self-driving, since the rural roads between wineries are the #1 safety fire; the Fiestas de la Vendimia (late Jul–late Aug) is the demand apex and sells out first.

faq.q: Can I see gray whales from Ensenada?
faq.a: Yes — offshore, December–April, peak January–March. Gray whales pass along the Pacific coast Ensenada→San Quintín on the longest mammal migration on earth; go with a licensed charter (life vests, weather-holds), noting the "friendly" lagoon nurseries lie farther south in Baja California Sur.

faq.q: When can I snorkel with sea lions at Los Islotes?
faq.a: September through May — the colony of 600+ California sea lions closes Jun 1–Aug 31 for pupping and mating, when operators substitute the San Rafaelito reef. It's a snorkel-only, no-touch encounter with a licensed operator, usually on a ~$100–150 full-day island tour.

faq.q: Can I stay overnight on Espíritu Santo?
faq.a: Only at Camp Cecil, a permitted 8-tent solar camp open Nov–Apr (2-night minimum) — there are no hotels, roads or cell service on this protected, uninhabited UNESCO island. Everyone else visits sunrise-to-sunset by permitted boat and carries everything in and out.

faq.q: How do I visit if the sea lions are closed?
faq.a: Come for the empty island itself — pink-cliff coves, white-sand beaches, kayak/SUP and the San Rafaelito reef snorkel that substitutes for Los Islotes in summer. Private crewed sailing charters (from ~$600+ per boat) are the calmest way to see it.

faq.q: What's the real risk on an uninhabited island?
faq.a: No services, no cell signal and no medical facilities. Any emergency requires a boat back to La Paz, then Hospital Salvatierra or private clinics with air-evac for major trauma — so carry travel medical + evacuation insurance and bring your own water, food and sun protection.

fcdo.note: THE FCDO'S DENMARK ADVISORY COVERS THE FAROE ISLANDS BY ITS OWN DECLARATION: "This travel advice also covers the Faroe Islands and Greenland." ⭐ THIS IS NOT A SUBSTITUTION. CC Jobs 96 and 97 recorded the Faroes as having no FCDO page and refused to assign Denmark's - which was the right refusal, because assigning a parent country's advisory to a self-governing territory is the inference the doctrine forbids. It turns out no assignment was needed: the source names its own scope. Corrected CC Job 100, 2026-08-20.
fcdo._absence_not_a_badge: Posture 1 means the FCDO names NO advisory against travel anywhere in this country. It is an ABSENCE. It is never a green badge, never a reassurance, and never a statement that this place is safe.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Fernando de Noronha?
faq.a: August–November is the dive peak because the dry season delivers the clearest water and calmest seas, with the September–October visibility apex reaching up to ~50 m. April–June (rainy) is the diver's value window — rain hits the surface, not the reef, so visibility stays strong and the island is quieter.

faq.q: How do you get to Baía do Sancho?
faq.a: Baía do Sancho is reached only by boat or by a staircase carved into the volcanic rock face, and a marine-park pass is required. It has been voted the best beach in the world by TripAdvisor travelers five times, which is why access is deliberately controlled.

faq.q: Which is the best honeymoon pousada on Fernando de Noronha?
faq.a: Pousada Maravilha is consistently ranked the island's top honeymoon hotel, with six sea-facing apartments plus bungalows with private hot tubs, an infinity pool, fine dining and a spa. Nannai Noronha (10 bungalows, private verandas, direct beach access) is the other ultra-tier couples pick.

faq.q: Can you swim with the spinner dolphins at Baía dos Golfinhos?
faq.a: No — Baía dos Golfinhos is a no-entry protected dolphin resting bay: no descending, no swimming, no boats inside. Spinner dolphins are watched from a clifftop viewpoint, best at first light. This is a legal protection, not a suggestion.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Remoteness and medical evacuation. Fernando de Noronha has a hyperbaric chamber adjacent to Hospital São Lucas, but the hospital provides basic emergency care only — serious trauma or complex decompression illness requires evacuation to the mainland (Recife/Natal), and weather can delay the flight. Carry insurance with medevac and dive conservatively.

faq.q: Is diving the Corveta Ipiranga wreck dangerous?
faq.a: It is technical / Extended-Range diving: the wreck sits at ~62 m off Ponta da Sapata, so operators require Nitrox plus ~50 logged dives and evaluation dives before permitting it, always with a pro. Recreational divers stay on shallower 8–22 m reef and cave sites. Because you leave only by air, observe an 18–24 h surface interval before your flight.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit the Brazilian side of Iguaçu Falls?
faq.a: March–April and August–September are the sweet spots — comfortable 20–30°C, still-high water from the summer rains, and far smaller crowds than the December–February peak; April–May is widely called the single best window, with near-full flow, cooled temperatures and thinned crowds.

faq.q: Why stay at the Belmond Hotel das Cataratas?
faq.a: Because it is the only hotel inside Brazil's Iguaçu National Park, its guests get the falls essentially alone — walking the trails before the 9am public opening and after the 5pm closing, the dawn-and-dusk private-falls access that no city hotel can match.

faq.q: What's worth doing besides the falls themselves?
faq.a: Two standouts extend the stay: the Itaipu Dam "Illuminated" night tour lights one of the world's largest hydroelectric plants with 747 spotlights and 112 luminaires, and Parque das Aves next to the park immerses you among 1,320+ birds across roughly 143 species.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for around the falls?
faq.a: The tri-border corridor: the Brazil–Argentina–Paraguay triple frontier is a known smuggling and money-laundering zone, but the Iguazu tourist corridor stays accessible with normal precautions — it's the Paraguay-side Ciudad del Este shopping run that carries elevated petty-crime and after-dark risk, so advise clients away from it unless escorted.

faq.q: Is the Macuco Safari boat trip dangerous?
faq.a: No, when run with the operator: it's a guided-only, three-stage run of roughly 1 hr 45 min (about 30 min on the water) with mandatory life vests issued at the dock — expect to get completely soaked, so leave anything not waterproof behind.

faq.q: How dangerous is diving Darwin and Wolf — can beginners do it?
faq.a: No — these are advanced dives, not a beginner destination. Reputable operators gate Darwin/Wolf on Advanced Open Water certification plus logged current/cold-water experience: divers hook onto ledges in ripping current at 20–30 m in 16–24 °C water, far from support. Gordon Rocks and Kicker Rock are the intermediate-to-advanced warm-ups.

faq.q: How long should I wait to fly after diving the Galápagos?
faq.a: Plan a full 18–24 hours before the island-to-mainland flight. A liveaboard week is repetitive multi-day diving (DAN: 18 h minimum, 24 h recommended), and Quito sits at ~2,850 m — so never book a same-day-as-last-dive flight. The only hyperbaric chamber is in Puerto Ayora, hours by boat from Darwin/Wolf, so DAN evacuation insurance is effectively mandatory.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive for hammerheads and whale sharks?
faq.a: June–November — the cool, plankton-rich season — is the big-animal window, with whale sharks peaking August–September, because the Humboldt upwelling drops water to 16–24 °C and concentrates pelagic life; ~90% of monitored hammerheads stay in the reserve then, schooling in the hundreds. Expect cooler water and stronger current.

faq.q: Do I need a cruise, or can I stay on land?
faq.a: Both work, but the iconic sites need a boat. Darwin and Wolf are liveaboard-only, and by park rule every visitor-site landing must be led by a licensed naturalist guide. Land-based island-hopping (Santa Cruz, Isabela) covers tortoises, Tortuga Bay and day dives; the deep wildlife (Española albatross, Genovesa seabirds) needs an expedition cruise.

faq.q: What's the best Galápagos trip for a honeymoon?
faq.a: A small all-suite expedition yacht or the highlands Pikaia Lodge. The warm season (Dec–May, water 25–27 °C, calm seas) is the easiest for first-timers and snorkeling; book 6–12 months ahead because the top cabins and suites — and holiday sailings — sell out first.

faq.q: Why is Granada worth visiting?
faq.a: Granada is the oldest city in Nicaragua and the oldest colonial city on the American mainland, settled in 1524 by conquistador Francisco Hernández de Córdoba. It claims to be the first European-established city on the mainland of the Americas, and its well-preserved colonial grid of pastel façades is the whole point of coming.

faq.q: What are the best outdoor things to do around Granada?
faq.a: The signature outings are volcanoes and water. Las Isletas — 365 islets flung into Lake Nicaragua by a Mombacho eruption — are toured by boat or kayak; Mombacho's cloud-forest is reached by 4x4 to a Crater Trail hike plus a canopy zip course; and Masaya's night tour puts you at a crater-rim platform above an active lava lake.

faq.q: Where's the best place to swim near Granada?
faq.a: Laguna de Apoyo, a crater lake about 25 minutes from Granada, is said to be the cleanest place to swim in all of Nicaragua because no motorboats are allowed on it. Day passes to lakeside spots run around $10 and include kayaks and loungers.

faq.q: Is Granada a good honeymoon destination?
faq.a: Yes, on paper it is a natural romance set — private-island lodges, rooftop sunsets over Cocibolca, pastel streets. The ultra anchor is Jicaro Island Lodge, a National Geographic Unique Lodge with 9 two-story "treehouse" casitas on a private Las Isletas islet, with lakeside yoga and three multi-course meals included.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Wrongful detention is the headline gatekeeper. Per the State Department, US nationals — including dual Nicaraguan-US citizens — are at serious risk of wrongful detention and may be held for years without due process, and authorities may seize property or search phones for anti-government content. A secondary risk is healthcare: comprehensive care exists only in Managua.

faq.q: Are the volcano hikes and lake trips dangerous?
faq.a: The activities themselves are guided and manageable, but they are content-only under the Level 3 advisory. Mombacho and Masaya are done with a park-authorized or licensed guide (volcanic-gas exposure and timed entry make it mandatory at Masaya), and Las Isletas boating requires lifejackets because Cocibolca can chop up fast.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Staying in the metro carve-out, not street crime. Fly into GDL (inside the carve-out), keep itineraries in the Guadalajara Metropolitan area, and don't self-drive onto the restricted southern-Jalisco highways (Hwy 110, Hwy 80). The city itself calls for standard big-city precautions; altitude is gentle at ~1,590 m.

faq.q: What is Guadalajara best known for culturally?
faq.a: Being the source of Mexico's soul exports. It is the birthplace of modern mariachi (heard in original context at Plaza de los Mariachis), the artisan-ceramics capital via Tlaquepaque and Tonalá (markets Thu + Sun at near-production prices), and home to the UNESCO-listed Instituto Cultural Cabañas with Orozco murals.

faq.q: Can I do a tequila day trip from Guadalajara?
faq.a: Yes — the José Cuervo Express. The train runs Saturdays (some Sundays) from the metro to Tequila town with open bar, agave fields and a distillery stop; Guadalajara is also the source of birria and tortas ahogadas. Use organized operators — do not self-drive after tasting.

faq.q: When is the mariachi festival, and is it worth planning around?
faq.a: Yes — it is the world's largest, in mariachi's birthplace. The Encuentro Internacional del Mariachi y la Charrería runs its 33rd edition Aug 26–Sep 6, 2026, with galas at Teatro Degollado; it and November's FIL book fair are the two hotel-compression peaks, so book those windows early.

faq.q: Is Colonia Americana worth a night out?
faq.a: Yes — it is repeatedly ranked among the world's coolest neighborhoods. The Chapultepec/Lafayette district anchors the metro's bar-and-restaurant density and its design-boutique hotels (Villa Ganz, Casa Habita, Hotel Demetria). Use rideshare or registered taxis at night, per standard big-city caution.

faq.q: Which Guanacaste beaches are best for calm swimming?
faq.a: Playa Hermosa and Playas del Coco anchor the calm-water belt. Blue Flag Playa Hermosa is quiet and low-key, and lively Playas del Coco — the region's oldest beach town, 30 minutes from LIR — is the dive, fishing and water-sports hub; both are amenity-rich swim beaches away from the open surf.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book a Guanacaste destination wedding?
faq.a: Book 12–18 months out for the most in-demand properties. Peak-season wedding dates at the top Guanacaste resorts fill 12–18 months in advance, and booking early also locks the best group room-block pricing before rates compress; plan 9–12 months minimum.

faq.q: Can you surf Witch's Rock and Ollie's Point from Tamarindo?
faq.a: Yes — both are boat-access breaks. Roca Bruja (Witch's Rock) inside Santa Rosa National Park is a world-class sand-bottom beach break and Ollie's Point is one of Costa Rica's best right-hand point breaks, reached on 1–2-hour open-water boat runs from Tamarindo, Coco or Flamingo.

faq.q: When can you dive with bull sharks at the Bat Islands?
faq.a: June through October is the window. The Bat Islands "Big Scare" is the only bull-shark dive in Costa Rica, where advanced divers descend with bull sharks up to 3+ metres; reliability peaks June–October and it runs as an advanced-cert charter out of Playas del Coco / Flamingo — a wildlife dive, not a guarantee.

faq.q: When is leatherback turtle nesting season at Playa Grande?
faq.a: Late October to mid-February, peaking December–January. Playa Grande / Las Baulas is the second-largest Pacific leatherback nesting beach on earth; ranger-led night tours run in that window with a 15-per-group cap for roughly $25 including entry and guide.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Pacific rip currents are the primary beach hazard. Guanacaste's open Pacific beaches carry rip currents and Tamarindo's surf adds board/reef injury risk, so swim at guarded or calm beaches like Conchal and Hermosa and take beginner surf only with a certified instructor.

faq.q: Is Bat Islands diving dangerous?
faq.a: It's advanced-only, not for new divers. The "Big Scare" requires a minimum PADI Advanced Open Water certification — strong shifting currents, thermoclines and 30 m+ depths — so enforce no-fly-after-diving (18 h single / 24 h repetitive) before any LIR/SJO flight and carry DAN cover.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: The southern-corridor highways, plus a steep city. The Level 3 driver is "huachicol" (oil-theft) violence along Hwy 45D and south — do not self-drive those routes. Otherwise the historic center is a compact walkable tourist zone; the practical caution is a very vertical, stepped city at **~2,000 m** (mild first-day altitude, sensible footwear, use the funicular).

faq.q: When is the Festival Cervantino, and how far ahead do I book?
faq.a: **Oct 7–25 in 2026** — and it sells out months ahead. It's Mexico's largest performing-arts festival and the single biggest compression window of the year; the booking curve builds ~4–6 months out at program/ticket release, so lock festival-and-hotel packages by late March / early April.

faq.q: What are the must-see culture sites?
faq.a: The UNESCO historic core (inscribed 1988): the Museo de las Momias (111 mummified bodies), the Diego Rivera birth-house, the Alhóndiga de Granaditas, the belle-époque Teatro Juárez, and the El Pípila funicular for the 360° city panorama.

faq.q: Is Guanajuato City romantic for couples?
faq.a: Strongly — it's the bookable-today SI. The signature ritual is the **callejoneada**, a lantern-lit roving serenade led by costumed student musicians up alleys too narrow for cars, wine in hand, ending near the Callejón del Beso (kiss on the third step); pair it with the El Pípila funicular (~30 MXN) at sunset.

faq.q: Is there good food?
faq.a: Yes — Bajío regional cuisine in a UNESCO setting: the mining-town enchiladas mineras and the café life of the Jardín de la Unión, with the Guanajuato wine route nearby, best done as a guided food walk.

faq.q: Should I stay in Guatemala City or head straight to Antigua?
faq.a: Treat Guatemala City as a 1–2-night stopover, not a leisure anchor. It's the international gateway — La Aurora (Central America's 4th-busiest, 4,919,850 pax in 2024) sits in Zone 13, ~45–60 minutes (~40–45 km) from Antigua — so most travelers rest a night, then road out to the country's true anchors.

faq.q: Is Guatemala City worth a stop for museums?
faq.a: Yes, for a half-day. The museum cluster is genuinely first-rate: Museo Popol Vuh holds one of the country's best pre-Hispanic and colonial-art collections, and Museo Ixchel holds ~8,000 textile pieces from 180+ Indigenous communities, both on the UFM campus in the safe Zone 10.

faq.q: How do I get from the airport safely?
faq.a: Use arranged or vetted transport, or Uber — never a street-hailed taxi. Move from La Aurora (Zone 13) to Zone 10/14 lodging on pre-arranged transport, avoid walking at night in unfamiliar zones, and ride the onward Antigua/Atitlán/Tikal handoff on a vetted shuttle or the DMC's own transport.

key_facts: Heavenly = Vail Resorts / Epic (since 2002); the one major resort that STRADDLES the California-Nevada state line (El Dorado + Alpine counties CA / Douglas County NV) above South Lake Tahoe

4,800 acres, 3,812 ft vertical (base 6,255 / summit 10,067); 97 trails (20% easier / 45% more difficult / 35% most difficult); 25 lifts incl a gondola + aerial tram + 2 six-packs + 8 HS quads; ~360 in snow; no night skiing
The Heavenly Gondola rises from Heavenly Village in downtown South Lake Tahoe; overlooks Lake Tahoe - the largest alpine lake in North America (6,225 ft surface, 1,645 ft deep, 2nd-deepest US lake)

STATELINE, NEVADA casinos at the base (unique ski-and-casino combo): Bally's Lake Tahoe, Caesars Republic Lake Tahoe (ex-Harveys, rebranded Jul 2025), Golden Nugget Lake Tahoe (ex-Hard Rock, 2023), Harrah's Lake Tahoe
US-TRAFFIC CANDOR: among Tahoe's most-visited but Vail reports visitation only in aggregate - no per-resort count published - consensus only
RNO ~55-60 mi / ~70 min (verify); Sacramento ~100 mi / ~2 hr via US-50; a dual-peak market (winter ski + big summer lake season)
NO on-site cat/heli (lift-served only; regional guided touring); NO natural hot springs at Heavenly (Grover Hot Springs, Markleeville ~35-45 min day-trip); Epic/lift prices dynamic
Nearest natural springs = Grover Hot Springs State Park (148F springs, 102-104F pool); Ritz-Carlton Lake Tahoe is at Northstar (separate resort), NOT Heavenly

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Holbox?
faq.a: Open-water seasickness, mosquitoes and hurricane timing — not crime. Whale-shark boats run into open ocean where swells cause common seasickness (take motion meds 30–60 min before departure); this is a mangrove island so dengue is active (use repellent); and the whale-shark peak (Jul–Aug) overlaps hurricane season (Jun–Nov, peak Aug–Oct), so insure the trip.

faq.q: When and how can I swim with whale sharks in Holbox?
faq.a: Between May 15 and Sep 17, peaking July–August, on a full-day morning boat departure with a CONANP-licensed operator. The encounter is snorkel-only beside the world's largest fish, with just two swimmers and a guide in the water at a time — book ahead during the event peak, as demand is high and operators are capped.

faq.q: What is Holbox like as a car-free island?
faq.a: It is a barefoot sandbar with sand streets and no cars — you arrive by ferry from Chiquilá and move around by golf cart or moped. That car-free rhythm is the point: it is the slow, bohemian antidote to Cancún, built for beach days, bikes and sunsets rather than nightlife strips.

faq.q: Is Holbox good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, for couples who want quiet design over resort scale. There are no mass all-inclusives — just artist-owned boutiques like Ser Casasandra (17 rooms + 1 villa) and Punta Caliza (12 rooms) — plus bioluminescent night swims at Punta Cocos. Because inventory is tiny, book 3–6 months ahead for the Dec–Apr peak.

faq.q: What else is there to do in Holbox beyond whale sharks?
faq.a: Plenty year-round. Walk the bioluminescent shore at Punta Cocos on new-moon nights, take the Cabo Catoche / Isla Pasión "three islands" boat-and-snorkel tour, kayak the mangroves, or ride the kite-surf season that starts in November — the reasons to come when the whale sharks are gone.

faq.q: What wildlife can I see in the Yum Balam reserve?
faq.a: A lot — Holbox sits inside the Yum Balam Flora & Fauna Protection Area, home to roughly 90% of the Yucatán's endemic bird species, plus flamingos, crocodiles and turtles. Guided eco or kayak tours through the protected mangroves are the way to see them; birdlife is seasonal, so ask what's present at your dates.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Holbox?
faq.a: December–April is the dry high season (blue skies, busiest); the whale-shark window is mid-May to mid-September. November is the underrated value pick — dry-season comfort, clean beaches and the start of kite season at low-season prices — while October is rainiest and many venues close. faq.q: What makes Hopkins different from Belize's other beach spots?
faq.a: It is a rare double-header: one of the very few points on the Caribbean where the barrier reef and the rainforest are visible from the same beach chair, on a 12-mile beach. Because the southern barrier reef here fronts a low-population mainland, South Water Caye Marine Reserve is one of the least-dived, healthiest reef systems in the country.

faq.q: Can you visit the jaguar preserve from Hopkins?
faq.a: Yes — Cockscomb Basin, the world's first jaguar preserve (128,000 acres, est. 1986), is about 30–40 minutes inland and works as a day trip, from an hour-long river stroll to a four-day Victoria Peak trek. The BZ$10 non-national entry fee is government pass-through; you book the guided day-tour for the value.

faq.q: Is Hopkins a good honeymoon destination?
faq.a: Yes, for jungle-and-reef romance rather than resort glitz. Hamanasi — a Tripadvisor Top-25-in-world honoree with 30 treehouse/beachfront rooms, a PADI facility and Green Globe certification — plus Belizean Dreams and Jaguar Reef Lodge are built around couples with private-guide adventures and infinity pools.

faq.q: Why is Hopkins the Garifuna cultural heart of Belize?
faq.a: Daily drum schools, homestays and food workshops make Hopkins the single most accessible stop to experience living Garifuna heritage — itself UNESCO-recognized intangible heritage (proclaimed 2001). Garifuna Settlement Day on November 19 brings a dawn Yurumein re-enactment and all-night drumming, and rooms in the village sell out.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Hopkins?
faq.a: Medical remoteness and mosquitoes, not crime. The State Dept warns emergency medical services are "usually unavailable or significantly delayed" and serious cases "normally require medical evacuation to another country," so evacuation-grade insurance is non-negotiable; the nearest hospital is Dangriga, with trauma routing to Belize City. Dengue is an active 2026 risk (2,794 cases in 2025), and jungle excursions raise exposure.

faq.q: Is the Mayflower Bocawina waterfall rappel or the jungle hiking dangerous?
faq.a: Mayflower Bocawina holds Belize's longest zipline (2.5 mi) and its only guided waterfall rappel (Antelope Falls, 250 ft) — certified guides and provided harness/helmet only, never solo. In Cockscomb, the Tiger Fern Trail now requires a guide (mandated after a hiker fatality) and Victoria Peak (3,675 ft) is dry-season-only and guide-mandatory.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in the water?
faq.a: Riptides on the open beaches, not the sheltered bays. The horseshoe coves (La Entrega, Maguey, San Agustín) are genuinely calm and swimmable, but open stretches of Tangolunda and Chahué carry rip currents — swim only the flagged, sheltered coves, and heed the flags.

faq.q: Which bays are calm enough for swimming and families?
faq.a: The horseshoe coves. La Entrega is the best land-accessible snorkel cove — the reef starts feet from shore — and Maguey, Órgano and San Agustín stay calm inside their coves; that's the difference from surf-driven Puerto Escondido up the coast.

faq.q: What's the one must-do day here?
faq.a: The nine-bays boat tour — a full-day (~7 h) expedition across the nine bays with beach and snorkel stops, bookable through Amstar's "Sea and Sun"/"Seven Bays" excursions or affiliate marketplaces (the National Park conservation bracelet is a cash pass-through).

faq.q: When can I see whales?
faq.a: Humpbacks run **Dec 15–Mar 21**, with sightings on **over 97% of tours** at the peak, on boat safaris out of Santa Cruz; dolphins and turtles are year-round, and turtle nesting (olive-ridley/green) runs Jul–Jan.

faq.q: Can beginners dive the reef here?
faq.a: Yes — the protected Pacific reef is beginner-friendly. La Entrega runs 10–12 m and San Agustín adds a ~30 m sunken ship for advanced divers, with up to ~18 m visibility in the dry season; book only PADI-certified operators (Huatulco Dive Center, Anfibios, Hurricane Divers).

faq.q: Is there culture beyond the beach?
faq.a: Yes — Copalita is one of only two seaside archaeological sites in Mexico (with Tulum), a Zapotec/Mixtec city settled by ~500 BC in rainforest above the river mouth, and La Crucecita's zócalo holds one of Mexico's largest Guadalupe ceiling murals.

faq.q: Is Huatulco good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, for calm-bay romance rather than branded-ultra. Secrets Huatulco is the adults-only, all-oceanfront-suite anchor of the Tangolunda strip; the coast tops out at premier all-inclusive plus a top oceanfront villa in Conejos — there is no Aman/Rosewood-tier hotel here.

faq.q: What's the best plan for a day at Iguazú Falls?
faq.a: Run the Devil's Throat first at the 08:00 park opening, then work back through the Upper and Lower Circuits. The park opens 08:00 and closes 18:00 with last falls access around 16:30, and starting at the Garganta station gives the best rainbow light and thinnest crowds; budget 5–6 hours minimum for all three circuits plus the Eco-Train.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Iguazú Falls?
faq.a: March–April and August–September are the sweet spot, because they balance strong water flow with comfortable 20–30 °C temperatures and manageable crowds. December–February brings maximum flow but heat above 35 °C and peak crowds, while May is a quiet sleeper month with autumn flow and room rates 30–40% below the Dec–Feb peak.

faq.q: Where should honeymooners stay at Iguazú?
faq.a: The two scarce in-jewel beds are the play: Awasi Iguazú (Relais & Châteaux, 14 stilted villas with a private guide and 4×4 each) and the Gran Meliá Iguazú, the only hotel inside the Argentine park. Both are near-zero on bedbanks and contract direct or via DMC, so book Awasi or an in-park falls-view room 6–12 months ahead.

faq.q: Should I visit the Brazilian side too — and what else is nearby?
faq.a: Yes if time allows: Argentina holds ~80% of the falls and the immersion, while Brazil's single panoramic boardwalk delivers the whole-system view as a passport-required border day-trip. South toward Posadas, the roofless red-sandstone cathedral of San Ignacio Miní (UNESCO-listed 1984) rounds out a cultural-heritage circuit.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for at Iguazú?
faq.a: Health and weather, not crime. Misiones province carries a CDC yellow-fever vaccination recommendation and a real dengue risk, so pack DEET and get a pre-travel vaccination consult; the catwalks are permanently misted and slippery, and extreme rainfall can close the Devil's Throat catwalk on river surge.

faq.q: Is the Gran Aventura speedboat dangerous?
faq.a: It is operator-run and low-risk with the rules followed, but not trivial. A life jacket is mandatory and a safety briefing is given before the 6 km run into the San Martín falls; jacket-quality reviews are mixed, so non-swimmers should weigh the run, everyone gets thoroughly soaked, and the trip is river-level-dependent and cancels in high water.

name: Ischgl
line: 239 km across two countries, a mountain that throws

key_facts: Silvretta Arena = cross-border Ischgl (AT) - Samnaun (CH, duty-free): 239 km pistes + 15 km ski routes, 45 lifts, base ~1,360-1,377 m to 2,872 m (Palinkopf/Greitspitze), ~1,512 m vertical
Piste split ~21% easy / 58% intermediate / 21% difficult; season ~27 Nov 2025 - 3 May 2026 (high, snow-sure)
Idalp = mid-mountain hub (lifts, restaurants, concert stage); ski across the border to duty-free Samnaun and back
Top of the Mountain concerts = stadium-scale acts on the mountain to open + close the season (artists/dates to verify)
Legendary apres/nightlife: Kitzloch + Niki's Stadl confirmed (Pacha/Kuhstall/Trofana Alm unverified)
Silvretta Arena VIP Skipass (EUR, covers both countries; prices to verify); no Ikon/Epic affiliation found

Hotel Trofana Royal = 5-star superior (Michelin Key 2026); Paznaunerstube (chef Martin Sieberer) Michelin-recognised + 4 G&M toques/18 pts (Michelin cross-check flagged); ~2,500 m2 spa (Falstaff 98/100)
Silvretta Therme Ischgl = modern village thermal-spa complex (opening year/size to verify)
Reached Innsbruck ~70 min / Zurich-Munich <3 hr; rail to Landeck-Zams then Paznaun bus
Heli-skiing NOT available at Ischgl - Austria permits it only at designated Vorarlberg (Lech-Zurs) sites, not Tirol/Paznaun
Big vertical ~1,512 m from 2,872 m to the village; 45-lift high-capacity network moves the winter crowds
Trofana Royal fields a 2nd gourmet room - Heimatbuehne (3 Gault&Millau toques / 16 pts) - beyond the Paznaunerstube
Cross-border avalanche: ski the Lawinenwarndienst Tirol bulletin for the Austrian side, SLF (Switzerland) for the Samnaun side
A rare four-in-one day: ski to duty-free Switzerland, shop, ski home, catch a mountain concert, close the night in the village

safety.emergency: 112 EU general / 140 Bergrettung alpine rescue / 144 ambulance / 133 police / 122 fire
safety.hospital: district hospital in the Landeck/Zams area (a.oe. Krankenhaus St. Vinzenz Zams) down-valley; 140 Bergrettung / helicopter alpine evac
safety.activity_note: High-alpine off-piste + 15 km ski routes - avalanche is the killer: Lawinenwarndienst Tirol via Euregio lawinen.report, EAWS 5-level scale; transceiver/shovel/probe + guide off-piste; Samnaun (Swiss) side falls under SLF - check the correct national bulletin per side; heli-skiing NOT available here (Austria restricts to Vorarlberg sites); pace alcohol at altitude; rescue 140 Bergrettung

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on an Isla Contoy trip?
faq.a: The open-water crossing and weather — not crime. Contoy sits ~30 km out at the seam where the Caribbean meets the Gulf, an exposed run where sea state can build and operators cancel trips in rough weather (especially hurricane season, Jun–Nov). Pick a calm-sea day, confirm the cancellation/reschedule policy, and keep life jackets on during transit.

faq.q: Is the reef snorkel and boat crossing dangerous?
faq.a: Both are low-risk with a guide, but respect the water. Snorkeling is snorkel-only with no decompression restriction — the real hazards are the open-water current at the reef seam, boat traffic and sun, so wear the vest, avoid all coral/wildlife contact and stay with the guide. On the ~30 km crossing, follow crew instructions and keep life jackets on.

faq.q: How do you actually visit Isla Contoy?
faq.a: Only through a handful of authorized operators — there is no independent access. The daily cap of 200 visitors makes it scarcity-priced, so book 3–6+ weeks ahead in peak season (1–3 weeks in shoulder); popular operators and calm-sea days fill first. Every trip bundles the park fee, lunch and snorkel gear.

faq.q: What is the Ixlaché reef snorkel like?
faq.a: It is the headline in-water stop — the northern start of the world's second-largest barrier reef. Ixlaché holds 17 hard and 14 soft coral species just south of the island; visibility is clearest in the dry season (Dec–Apr), and the snorkel is included in the guided tour on calm-sea days.

faq.q: What wildlife will I see on Isla Contoy?
faq.a: Birds above all — the island is critical habitat for 173+ species, with frigatebird and pelican colonies you pass on the marked trails. Green and loggerhead sea turtles nest on the beaches May–October, adding a seasonal wildlife hook; the whole reserve is car-free and strictly protected.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Isla Contoy, and where do trips leave from?
faq.a: December–April brings the calmest seas and clearest Ixlaché water; the summer whale-shark run (roughly Jun–Sep) is the true event peak, since Contoy is often sold as a whale-shark + Contoy combo. Trips depart Cancún and Isla Mujeres marinas on ~7–8 hour days — there is no lodging, so base off-island.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on Isla Mujeres?
faq.a: Water, weather and currents — not crime. Drink bottled water, use repellent for dengue (no malaria in the tourist zone), and note hurricane season runs June–November with September riskiest. Playa Norte is comparatively sargassum-protected, but 2026 is heavy region-wide; the Punta Sur loggerhead dives sit in strong currents, so they are for advanced divers only.

faq.q: Is swimming with whale sharks or diving Punta Sur dangerous?
faq.a: The whale-shark encounter is snorkel-only with no decompression restriction — wear the vest, no touching, stay with the guide against boat traffic and open-water current. Punta Sur's summer loggerhead dive is a strong-current drift for advanced divers with a local guide; observe no-fly of 18–24 hours after any scuba.

faq.q: When and how can I swim with whale sharks from Isla Mujeres?
faq.a: Roughly June to September, on a snorkel-only boat excursion to the aggregation — the island is the whale-shark snorkel capital of the region. Tours book about 30–39 days out on average and sell out fast in peak summer, so reserve at least 3–6 weeks ahead; it is snorkel-only, with no scuba allowed.

faq.q: Can beginners dive MUSA from Isla Mujeres?
faq.a: Yes — MUSA is one of the most accessible dives anywhere. Its 470+ statues sit just 3.5–8 m down, shallow enough for Open Water divers and snorkelers, and at ≤9 m these are easy day dives. Advanced divers can add the Punta Sur loggerhead drift in summer, which sits in strong current and is guided-only.

faq.q: Is Playa Norte good, and will sargassum ruin it?
faq.a: It is the island's signature beach — waist-deep, glass-calm turquoise you can wade out a hundred meters into — and one of the most sargassum-protected stretches in the region. In a heavy year like 2026 that protection is a genuine edge, but still disclose: no beach is fully immune, and mornings are cleanest.

faq.q: Why is Izamal called the Yellow City, and what makes it special?
faq.a: It is Mexico's first Pueblo Mágico (designated 2002), and the entire historic center is painted one standardized ochre-gold — a color tradition set for Pope John Paul II's August 1993 visit and maintained ever since. The city is built in layers: the Spanish set the great Franciscan convent atop a Maya temple, and the Kinich Kakmó sun-god pyramid still rises above the rooftops.

faq.q: Can you climb the pyramid in Izamal?
faq.a: Yes — Kinich Kakmó is climbable to the summit, which sets it apart from Chichén Itzá, where El Castillo has been closed to climbers since 2008. The ~200 × 180 m pyramid dates to c. 400–600 AD; the steps are steep, uneven Maya risers with no handrails, so wear sturdy shoes and mind your footing on the descent.

faq.q: Is Izamal good for a romantic day or honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — it is a golden-hour romance magnet. The convent glows like a lantern above the plaza at sunset, a 45–60 min horse-drawn calesa ride winds through the yellow arcades, and the light seems to come from the buildings themselves. Most couples day-trip it from Mérida (70 km / ~1h10) or book one night in an in-town boutique to shoot the convent at golden hour.

faq.q: What is there to do beyond the convent?
faq.a: Hands-on Maya craft: the Centro Cultural y Artesanal runs artisan workshops and tours to hammock weavers, huipil embroiderers and alebrije painters who often work in-shop while you eat. Yucatecan cuisine and Hanal Pixán (the Maya Day of the Dead food tradition) give a soft culinary layer for later.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Izamal?
faq.a: Heat and footing, not crime. The shadeless plazas and the exposed, handrail-free Kinich Kakmó climb get hot at midday, so carry water, a hat and sunscreen and shoot golden hour rather than noon. Izamal has local clinics only — the nearest full trauma care is Mérida, ~1h10 west.

name: Jackson Hole
line: Ride Big Red to the top of America's steepest

key_facts: JHMR = Teton Village, WY; INDEPENDENT (Kemmerer family since 1992); on the FULL Ikon Pass ONLY (not Base/Session) + ALL Ikon holders must make advance lift reservations (days may sell out)

Base 6,311 / summit 10,450 ft (Rendezvous Mtn); VERTICAL 4,139 ft (one of the biggest in the US); 2,500 in-bounds acres + ~3,000 backcountry-access; terrain ~10% beg / 40% int / 50% expert; ~450+ in snow; no night skiing

The Aerial Tram 'Big Red' (100-pax, ~9 min, current tram Dec 2008) climbs to Rendezvous; Corbet's Cabin summit waffles; CORBET'S COULOIR = expert chute with a committing ~10-20 ft cornice entry, then an expert run (not a sustained death-pitch)

Jackson Hole Airport (JAC) = the ONLY commercial airport inside a US national park (Grand Teton); ~7 mi N of Jackson town, ~28 min to Teton Village; RESORT (Teton Village) is distinct from the TOWN of Jackson (~12 mi)
US-TRAFFIC CANDOR: high-visitation/high-spend/capacity-constrained (Ikon reservations + sell-outs) but no per-resort count published - consensus only

Guiding + heli are INDEPENDENT, NOT resort-run: Jackson Hole Mountain Guides (AMGA-accredited, est. 1968) for backcountry/AIARE; heli via a separate third-party outfitter (operator unverified); NO resort cat/heli
A two-national-park basecamp: Grand Teton adjacent + Yellowstone ~1.5 hr N; National Elk Refuge (~25,000 ac, ~7,500 elk, winter sleigh rides); big summer season

NO natural hot springs at Teton Village (Granite Hot Springs - winter snowmobile access; Astoria Hot Springs - reservations; both day-trips); Ikon/lift prices dynamic; Amangani closed for refurbishment (verify)

safety.hospital: St. John's Health, 625 East Broadway, Jackson (~12 mi from Teton Village) - full-service 24/7 ER; higher-level trauma out of valley (trauma level verify)
safety.activity_note: ALTITUDE (base 6,311 ft, summit 10,450 ft - tram tops 10,000 fast; hydrate, ease alcohol, descend if AMS worsens); AVALANCHE life-safety spine (in-bounds patrolled/controlled; boundary gates + ~3,000 ac backcountry severe) - Bridger-Teton Avalanche Center (BTAC), Tetons zone (also Snake River/Salt River & Wyoming Ranges/Togwotee) - confirm zone label; beacon/probe/shovel + guide (JHMG), never duck ropes; CORBET'S + steep chutes = no-fall zones (committing entries; respect closures); TETON PASS (WY-22, summit 8,431 ft, Glory Bowl slide paths) - WYDOT early-morning avalanche-control closures, >60 mi detour when closed; tree-wells; cold + intense UV; keep wildlife distance in the parks

faq.q: When is the best time to kitesurf in Jericoacoara?
faq.a: July–December is kite season because the dry-season trade wind blows nearly every day, running ~20–25 kt and building to 30–35 kt on September–November afternoons (strongest in November). This wind is the demand engine, so book schools and pousadas early — the curve switches on around late June / early July.

faq.q: What is there to do in Jericoacoara besides the beach?
faq.a: The signature rituals are free and natural: climb the Sunset Dune (Duna do Pôr do Sol) at dusk to watch the sun drop straight into the Atlantic — one of the few places in Brazil where it does — walk ~45 minutes to the Pedra Furada arch, and float in the wooden hammocks set in the shallows of crystal-clear Lagoa do Paraíso.

faq.q: Is Jericoacoara good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, but set expectations at barefoot-luxe, not palace-luxury — exquisite bungalows, sand floors and candlelight. Vila Kalango (24 beachfront bungalows, MICHELIN Guide) anchors the lane, and the green Feb–May shoulder sells the quiet, glassy-lagoon honeymoon version when the pousadas discount.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Remoteness. Jeri is road-less, so definitive trauma care and complex medical evacuation route through Fortaleza — a 4x4-only, ~4–5 hr ground leg (or JJD air) — then international air evac as needed. Factor that into any emergency-response estimate; travel insurance with medical-evacuation cover is strongly advised.

faq.q: Is kitesurfing in Jericoacoara dangerous?
faq.a: Manageable with the right school: use IKO-certified schools (Rancho do Peixe/Ticowind, Preá Kite Club, North Kite Center, BLU). Central-Jeri offshore wind is not for beginners — they route to Preá's flat water — and deep-water sessions warrant a life jacket, with a local briefing mandatory because of open-water current.

name: Keystone
line: Colorado's biggest night skiing and the ultimate family mountain

key_facts: Keystone = Vail Resorts / Epic; three mountains (Dercum, North Peak, The Outback) + Bergman/Erickson bowls; ~3,148 acres; vertical 3,128 ft (base 9,280 / summit 12,408); 21 lifts incl 2 gondolas
LARGEST night-skiing operation in Colorado (up to 15 lit trails + A51 park to 7 p.m.); A51 ~60-acre terrain park
~230 in (~5.8 m) snowfall + 660+ ac snowmaking; typically one of the first US resorts to open (25 Oct 2025) to ~5 Apr 2026
FAMILY-first: Kids Ski Free (12 & under, 2+ nights) + free Kidtopia (cookie time, parade, fireworks) + world's largest mountaintop snow fort
CAT-SKIING HAS ENDED: the Bergman/Erickson bowls are now LIFT-SERVED by the Bergman Bowl Express (2023-24), 550+ ac in-bounds; no active paid cat-ski program
Purpose-built base-village complex (River Run + Mountain House/Lakeside) - NOT a historic town; no natural hot springs on-site (nearest ~1 hr)
US-TRAFFIC CANDOR: ~#9 nationally / ~1.4M is industry consensus, not operator-published
Fine dining Alpenglow Stube (11,444 ft) + Ski Tip Lodge (1800s prix-fixe); new upscale Kindred Resort (2025-26); DEN ~90 mi via I-70; ~14 mi to Breckenridge (not 6)

faq.q: Where can I trek chimps instead, right now?
faq.a: Rwanda - Nyungwe Forest (US L3, bookable). It is the direct live twin - chimpanzee trekking on a $250 permit, plus the canopy walk and colobus troops - the responsible live choice while Uganda is on the Ebola hold. We route all chimp demand there.

faq.q: Will this clear - should I wait for Kibale?
faq.a: Possibly - this is a health-driven, dynamic advisory (an outbreak, not conflict), so it can be lifted when the outbreak is contained. We re-verify Uganda's status every publish cycle and will flip Kibale to bookable the moment it drops below Level 4. For a firm 2026 chimp trek, book Nyungwe now.

faq.q: What would Kibale offer when it reopens?
faq.a: The primate capital of the world - up to 1,500 chimps and 13 primate species, the $250 chimp trek (and the full-day ~$300 Habituation Experience), plus the Bigodi wetland birding walk. All held until the advisory lifts.

faq.q: Is Kibale a safari (big-game) destination?
faq.a: No - it is a rainforest of primates, not a savanna, so big-game safari is a documented miss; the draw is the chimp and primate trek (a Global Adventures product), exactly like Rwanda's Nyungwe. For Big game, we route to Kenya, Tanzania or Akagera.

faq.q: What are the non-Ebola health requirements for Uganda?
faq.a: Yellow fever is mandatory for entry (all travelers >=1 yr, checked at Entebbe, vaccinate >=10 days before); malaria prophylaxis is essential (all regions); carry AMREF Flying Doctors + insurance. All moot while the L4 hold stands.

name: Killington
line: The Beast of the East

key_facts: Killington = 'The Beast of the East', the LARGEST ski area in the eastern US; six interconnected peaks (Killington, Snowdon, Skye, Ramshead, Bear, Sunrise); 1,509 acres, 155 trails (212 incl affiliated Pico Mountain, same pass)

New England's BIGGEST vertical (3,050 ft) off a 4,229-ft summit (Killington Peak; 2nd-highest in the Green Mtns); base 1,165 ft; K-1 Express + Skyeship gondolas among 21 lifts; ~250 in snow + ~71% snowmaking
LONGEST SEASON IN THE EAST: typically late Oct-late May (200+ days), first open (October) + last to close (Superstar into May/June via snowmaking); the 'King of Spring'

OWNERSHIP CORRECTED: no longer Powdr - bought by the local Killington Independence Group on 27 Sep 2024 (Powdr retained a minority stake); on the Ikon Pass (Beast 365 Pass includes Ikon Base; full-Ikon upgrade available)

Stifel Killington Cup = FIS Alpine WORLD CUP (women's GS + slalom) on Superstar every Thanksgiving weekend since 2016 (one of few US World Cup races; Shiffrin won slalom the first 5 editions); FIS confirms 28-29 Nov 2026
US-TRAFFIC CANDOR: among the most-visited Eastern resorts but no per-resort count published - consensus only

Killington Road ('the Access Road') = a genuine apres/nightlife strip (The Wobbly Barn); closest commercial airport Rutland (RUT, Cape Air to Boston ~40 min); Boston + NY/NJ drive market; ~15 mi from Rutland

NO on-site cat/heli (fully lift-served); NO natural hot springs (none in region); NO avalanche center (low-avalanche Eastern terrain - ice/cold/driving spine); MID-MARKET (not ultra-luxury); Ikon/lift prices dynamic; summer bike park + golf + Beast Mountain Coaster

safety.hospital: Rutland Regional Medical Center, Rutland (~15 mi) - 144 beds, largest community hospital in Vermont, full 24/7 emergency department
safety.activity_note: NO AVALANCHE CENTER governs Killington (low-avalanche, patrolled, lift-served Eastern terrain - do NOT cite CAIC/UAC/BTAC/GNFAC); ALTITUDE is LOW (summit 4,229 ft - AMS not a factor); the winter spine is ICE/HARDPACK ('Eastern ice'/boilerplate - sharp edges, ski in control), extreme COLD + WIND CHILL on the exposed summit (frostbite/hypothermia - layer, cover skin, warm-up breaks), and VERMONT WINTER DRIVING (US-4, VT-100, the steep Killington Road/Access Road - winter tires/chains, check VTrans 511vt.com); tree-wells in glades; terrain-park risk at Bear

name: Kiroro
line: Hokkaido's quiet powder vault

key_facts: Snow-sure inland Hokkaido powder resort in Akaigawa Village, Yoichi District; ~70 min from Sapporo, ~45 min Otaru, ~90 min New Chitose Airport
~20 m (2,000 cm) average annual snowfall — among Hokkaido's deepest; season early Dec-early May
30 km of piste (8.6 km easy 29% / 10.6 km intermediate 35% / 10.8 km difficult 36%); base 520 m, summit 1,180 m, vertical 660 m
Three peaks: Asari 1,180 m, Nagamine 1,090 m, Yoichi 900 m; 10 lifts incl. Kiroro Gondola; ~24 trails; ~4 km top-to-bottom cruiser; 152 ha
14 sanctioned in-bounds tree-run zones (Powder Ridge, Deep Pine, Monkey Park) + backcountry gates; night skiing 'Nighter' from JPY 2,900; adult day pass JPY 8,800
Club Med Kiroro Peak (adults/12+, Exclusive Collection from Winter 2025, 11 included activities, Club Med Spa, onsen, ski-in/ski-out)
Club Med Kiroro Grand (families from age 2, kids clubs 0-10 + teen 11-17, 13 included activities, onsen + rotenburo, Japanese-French dining)
Yu Kiroro luxury residences: 108 freehold ski-in/ski-out units (studios to 3-bed + 2 penthouses), hot-spring onsen, 24-hr fitness, ski valet, Yukashi restaurant

safety.emergency: 110 police / 119 fire + ambulance / 118 Japan Coast Guard (free 24/7; mountain rescue via 110/119)
safety.hospital: Nearest hospitals Otaru (~45 min); major trauma Sapporo (~70 min); confirm specific ED (verify)
safety.activity_note: Deep-snow winter sports: off-piste/backcountry avalanche risk (check JAN nadare.jp Yoichi/Kiroro bulletin; transceiver/shovel/probe + guide), tree-well/deep-snow immersion suffocation, cold/whiteout/frostbite; rescue 110/119

name: Kitzbühel
line: The medieval Gamsstadt where the world's most feared downhill

key_facts: The Streif downhill: 3,312 m long, 860 m vertical (start 1,665 m, finish 805 m); Mausefalle 85% (40.4deg), 80 m jumps, up to 150 km/h; record 1:51.58 (Fritz Strobl, 1997)
Hahnenkamm Races: 86th ran 23-25 Jan 2026 (Franzoni won the downhill 1:52.31); 87th runs 18-24 Jan 2027; finish arena draws 80,000+
KitzSki: 188 km slopes (102 easy / 66 intermediate / 20 difficult) + 45 km ski routes, 58 lifts, base 800 m to summit 2,000 m; rated 4.9-star World-class
2025/26 season 7 Nov 2025-12 Apr 2026; adult day pass ~EUR 79.50 premium season
3S Bergbahn (opened Jan 2005): 3,642 m long, cabins hang up to 400 m above ground, 24-person cabins, 3,200 pph, ~9-min crossing
Medieval walled town granted town rights 6 June 1271 (Duke Ludwig II of Bavaria); historic centre 750+ years old; 'Monte Carlo of the Alps'
Town at 762 m, population ~8,272; railway arrived 1875
Four championship golf courses + 500 km (311 mi) hiking trails + 120 km (75 mi) MTB paths; five-stars incl. Tennerhof, Grand Tirolia, A-ROSA
