faq.q: What is the current advisory for Komodo, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Indonesia at Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution (reissued 30 April 2025). Its only Level 4 (Do Not Travel) carve-outs are Central Papua (Papua Tengah) and Highland Papua (Papua Pegunungan), for civil unrest; Komodo, in East Nusa Tenggara, sits well apart from both. The material regional flag comes from the UK FCDO, which advises against all travel within 7 km of the crater of Mount Lewotobi Laki-Laki on Flores - a volcano that erupted on 17 June 2025, holds Indonesia's highest alert (level 4), and carries mud/debris-flow warnings plus disruption to flights to and from Bali and Flores. Because Labuan Bajo, Komodo's gateway, is on Flores, build slack into flight connections and confirm status before travel. Carry DAN membership plus separate dive-accident insurance and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Since 13 October 2018 Komodo's gateway has had its own chamber: a hyperbaric oxygen chamber at Siloam Hospitals Labuan Bajo (Flores), the first in East Nusa Tenggara and an eight-patient chamber, so divers no longer have to be flown to Bali first. The fallback remains Sanglah General Hospital in Denpasar, Bali, roughly 1.5 hours by air. Confirm the Labuan Bajo chamber's 24-hour readiness on your dates with the operator or DAN, and note that the Mount Lewotobi flight disruption can affect the Bali evacuation leg. Komodo's currents put a premium on conservative profiles and dive-accident insurance.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Komodo?
faq.a: May-October, the Southeast Monsoon dry season, is the popular liveaboard window, with northern waters at 30C and optimal visibility. The cooler southern sites (Manta Alley area) carry more nutrient and colder water; route and month are set by the operator's north/south plan.

faq.q: Where do I see mantas in Komodo?
faq.a: Manta Alley and Manta Point are the named manta sites - cleaning stations and feeding aggregations in current.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Castle Rock and Crystal Rock are high-current pinnacle dives suited to experienced divers with reef hooks; sheltered sites and the Sangeang volcanic slopes suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards. Dive within your certification and the briefing.

faq.q: Can I see the Komodo dragons on the same trip?
faq.a: Yes - Komodo National Park pairs the diving with ranger-guided dragon walks on Komodo and Rinca and the Padar viewpoint; most liveaboards include a park day.

faq.q: How far ahead do Komodo liveaboards book?
faq.a: Peak dry-season (May-October) weeks on preferred vessels fill earliest; hold roughly 3-9 months out for peak windows, nearer term for the shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

faq.q: Can you climb Arenal Volcano?
faq.a: No — you cannot summit Arenal, because it is an active volcano. The hikeable product is the Arenal 1968 Trail and the National Park loops, walking hardened lava flows with lake-and-cone views; the active cone itself is closed to hikers.

faq.q: Which Arenal hot springs are best for couples?
faq.a: Ecotermales Fortuna is the romantic pick. It is intimate and capacity-capped — romantic, not a waterpark — at a $59 timed pass, a better couples fit than the larger complexes like Baldi ($85), The Springs ($75) or Tabacón (~$99–110).

faq.q: How hot are the Arenal hot springs?
faq.a: They run roughly 90–104°F. The mineral water is heated by the volcano itself, and the region's best springs have been built around by high-end resorts, rustic lodges and luxury hotels — hydrate, limit soak time and go easy on alcohol in the heat.

faq.q: Is the Arenal volcano dangerous to visit?
faq.a: No — Arenal is an active but monitored volcano, and guided viewing is the whole point. The one hard rule is no summit hikes on the active cone; only the 1968 Trail, Cerro Chato-area and National Park loops are open to hikers.

faq.q: When and how can I swim with whale sharks in La Paz?
faq.a: October 1 to April 30, on a licensed half-day snorkel in the bay's protected refuge zone — never scuba. Encounters are capped at 5 swimmers plus a certified guide per shark for 30 minutes, with no touching, to protect the juveniles that feed there.

faq.q: Is La Paz a good island and beach base?
faq.a: Yes — it is the launch port for the whole Sea-of-Cortez set: protected Balandra, Tecolote, the Malecón waterfront and boat trips to UNESCO-listed Espíritu Santo. It's the quiet, low-key alternative to the Los Cabos corridor two hours south.

faq.q: What is there to dive around La Paz?
faq.a: The signature dive is the Salvatierra, a 1976 ferry wreck at 18–20 m that's now a thriving artificial reef, diveable near year-round, plus the El Bajo seamount. La Paz has its own recompression chamber (confirm status at booking) and DAN emergency is +1-919-684-9111.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Missing the season, not crime. Whale sharks are gone May–Sep, sea lions close Jun 1–Aug 31, both are snorkel-only (no touch, no scuba), and hurricane season runs Jun–Nov. Book the Oct–Apr window ahead and carry trip insurance for summer/fall.

name: La Plagne
line: France's great family mountain

key_facts: Half of PARADISKI (~425 km, ~160 lifts, with Les Arcs + Peisey-Vallandry, linked by the double-decker Vanoise Express since 2003); La Plagne own domain ~225 km (62% easy / 26% int / 12% diff)

Eleven villages - high stations (Plagne Centre, Belle Plagne, Aime 2000 ~2,100 m) + valley villages (Champagny-en-Vanoise, Montchavin, Les Coches); Bellecote glacier high point ~3,250 m (skiresort 3,167 - flag)
Named the MOST-VISITED ski resort in the world in 2014 (2.5M+ visitors/season) - carry as 'one of the world's most-visited', not a current-year superlative

FRANCE'S ONLY Olympic bobsleigh track (1992 Albertville; beneath Plagne 1800; 1,500 m/19 turns): public Bob Raft (~EUR 57, ~80 km/h, from 1.30 m), Speed Luge (~137, ~90 km/h, 16+), Bob Racing (~149, ~120 km/h, pro pilot); mid-Dec-end March; reused for 2030 Olympics
One of France's premier FAMILY resorts (gentle wide pistes, ski-to-door villages, huge activity roster); the 4-star Araucaria (84 rooms, Spa NUXE) the marquee hotel in an apartment/chalet market
Season ~mid-Dec-late Apr (opens 12 Dec 2026); rail Aime-la-Plagne/Moutiers/Landry; airports Geneva/Grenoble ~149 km, Lyon ~196 km (times verify); US pass affiliation NOT documented - do not assert
AVALANCHE MASSIF UNCERTAIN (Vanoise vs Beaufortain) - flagged, not guessed; Meteo-France BERA 5-level
HELI-SKIING BANNED IN FRANCE - guided touring/glacier off-piste only; NO natural hot springs (nearest thermal Brides-les-Bains, off-domain - verify)

safety.emergency: 112 (Europe) / 15 SAMU / 17 police / 18 fire / 114 SMS; mountain rescue via 112 / PGHM (Bourg-Saint-Maurice) + resort pisteurs-secouristes
safety.hospital: Resort clinics; hospitals Bourg-Saint-Maurice / Moutiers + CHAM Albertville-Moutiers; trauma Chambery / Grenoble / Annecy; heli evac SMUR/PGHM (verify)
safety.activity_note: High-alpine winter sports: off-piste + Bellecote glacier avalanche risk - Meteo-France BERA, 5-level scale, MASSIF UNCERTAIN (Vanoise vs Beaufortain - confirm, do not guess); transceiver/shovel/probe + UIAGM guide; NO heli-skiing (banned in France) - guided touring only; glacier/crevasse (~3,250 m) guided; OLYMPIC BOB rides 80-120 km/h (~3G) - age/height limits, follow staff; altitude/sun (cat-3/4 protection); rescue 112/PGHM

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Laikipia?
faq.a: The on-foot and on-horse activities, and remoteness. Laikipia's draw is walking, horseback and night safaris among dangerous game - inherently higher-risk than a vehicle; go only with the armed conservancy guides and follow instruction. The plateau is remote, so carry AMREF Flying Doctors (~$40 pp/30 days) + travel-medical insurance.

faq.q: Where do I see rhino - and the last two northern whites?
faq.a: At Ol Pejeta (the last two northern white rhinos, Najin and Fatu, in a guarded 700-acre enclosure, plus East Africa's largest black-rhino population) and Lewa (~12% of Kenya's black rhino, plus Grevy's zebra) - the best rhino viewing in Kenya, and a genuine conservation story.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Laikipia?
faq.a: Jun/Jul-Oct and Dec-Mar (dry) are best, but the high plateau delivers year-round - a strong choice when the migration parks are at their peak-price crush. The green season is lush, quiet and better value.

faq.q: What can I do in Laikipia that I can't in the national parks?
faq.a: Because it's private conservancy land: horseback safaris, walking safaris, night drives, lion tracking, mountain biking, camel treks and star beds - the active, immersive safari the parks don't allow, with a fraction of the vehicles.

faq.q: Do I need a visa or yellow-fever certificate for Kenya?
faq.a: An eTA (Kenya replaced visas with the eTA in 2024 - apply at least 2 weeks ahead). Yellow fever is compulsory only if you arrive from a YF-risk country; CDC recommends the vaccine for most.

key_facts: Volcanic caldera lake at 1,562 m (5,125 ft), up to 340 m deep, ~130 km², ringed by three volcanoes — San Pedro, Tolimán, Atitlán (Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Atitlán, Accessed 2026-07-06)

Villages divide by role: Panajachel gateway hub, San Pedro backpacker/Spanish-school, San Marcos yoga/wellness, Santiago Atitlán largest/traditional, San Juan weaving + coffee (Source: adventurouskate.com, Accessed 2026-07-06)
Indian Nose sunrise hike (~30 min pre-dawn) is the signature caldera overlook; San Marcos offers yoga retreats + Cerro Tzankujil cliff-jump (Source: adventurouskate.com, Accessed 2026-07-06)
Dry season Nov–Apr is most photogenic; Christmas + Semana Santa fill weeks ahead; Sept–Oct rates 40–50% below peak (Source: atitlan.com, Accessed 2026-07-06)

Air access via GUA (La Aurora Intl) + shuttle/private transfer ~3 hr to Panajachel; boat (lancha) is the only road between villages (Source: theabroadblog.com / adventurouskate.com, Accessed 2026-07-06)

faq.q: What's the Indian Nose sunrise hike, and can you climb the volcanoes?
faq.a: The Indian Nose (Nariz del Indio) is a ~30-minute pre-dawn ridge trek to a panoramic caldera-and-three-volcano overlook "in perfect silence" — Atitlán's signature dawn. You can also summit the harder volcanoes (San Pedro ~3,020 m, Atitlán ~3,535 m), which reach real altitude, so go guided-only.

faq.q: Where do you stay for a honeymoon at Lake Atitlán?
faq.a: At the lake's one true-luxury anchor: Casa Palopó, Guatemala's only Relais & Châteaux hotel — a ~15-room boutique above Santa Catarina Palopó with three-volcano views. Beneath it sit eco-luxury Laguna Lodge and full-staff cliffside private villas with private docks, ideal for honeymoons and small buyouts.

faq.q: When is the Chichicastenango market?
faq.a: Thursdays and Sundays only. It's Guatemala's most famous Maya market — textiles, masks, produce, the Santo Tomás church and the hillside Pascual Abaj shrine — booked as a guided day-trip from Atitlán, because those are the two K'iche' Maya trading days that drive the weekly highland micro-peak.

faq.q: Is Lake Atitlán good for a yoga retreat?
faq.a: Yes — San Marcos La Laguna is Central America's best-known yoga village, with retreat centers like Las Pirámides del Ká and Eagle's Nest plus a cluster of vegetarian cafés and a genuine decades-old community. Retreats run set calendars, so wellness bookings often carry a 2–6-month lead.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on the lake?
faq.a: The wind, not the water quality. The Xocomil — a Pacific-vs-northern wind collision — kicks up late morning and afternoon and is "capable of capsizing boats," so cross early on licensed lanchas with life vests. Separately, verify the current cyanobacteria (Microcystis) swim advisory before booking lake-swim.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for at Lake Manyara?
faq.a: Not the parks - the advisory's concerns are the far-southern Mtwara Region (terrorism, far away) and city petty crime, plus a flagged LGBTQ+ targeting concern travelers should weigh (Tanzanian law criminalizes same-sex relations). In Manyara itself the risks are ordinary safari ones: stay in-vehicle near game, keep clear of the large baboon troops, malaria prophylaxis.

faq.q: Are the tree-climbing lions guaranteed?
faq.a: No sighting is ever guaranteed - the tree-climbing behaviour is famous but sporadic - yet Manyara is the one park in Tanzania where it happens regularly, and even without it the park's flamingos, forest, elephants and Rift-wall scenery justify the stop.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Lake Manyara?
faq.a: For game and the tree-climbing lions, the dry season Jun-Oct; for the flamingo spectacle and birding, the wetter Nov-Jun when the lake fills and the algae blooms draw the biggest flocks. It's a rewarding stop year-round.

faq.q: Is Manyara worth more than a half-day?
faq.a: For most itineraries it's a half-day or overnight gateway stop en route to Ngorongoro - that's the right dose for a compact park - but birders and photographers happily give it a full day for the forest, the lake hide and the escarpment light.

faq.q: Do I need a visa or yellow-fever certificate for Tanzania?
faq.a: eVisa required - apply on the official portal before departure. Yellow fever is not required direct from the US/Europe, but is mandatory if you transit >12 h through a risk country like Kenya.

faq.q: Are the Uros, Taquile and Amantaní islands worth it — and does my money reach the families?
faq.a: Yes, and this is the reason to come. Booked through the community co-op, an Amantaní overnight homestay costs roughly $10–15 per person including meals and rotates through ten host communities, so the income reaches families directly rather than mainland middlemen — the deepest cultural experience on the lake.

faq.q: How hard is the island walking, and what should I plan for?
faq.a: Plan for altitude, not difficulty. Island hikes run ~3,800–4,100 m — Taquile is a steady 30–60 minute uphill from the dock, and Amantaní's twin temple hills top near 4,100 m — so the real risk is AMS. Arrive already acclimatized, pace the climb, and carry water.

faq.q: Is Lake Titicaca good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, as a quiet luxe add-on to a Cusco/Machu Picchu core. The standout is Titilaka, an 18-suite all-inclusive Relais & Châteaux lodge on a private peninsula with lake-view suites, a private jetty and oxygen-quiet calm — sunrise over the water and private catamaran sailing.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Altitude — full stop. At ~3,810 m the lake is the highest stop on most Peru circuits, higher than Cusco, so AMS (soroche) is the dominant safety fact and outranks crime by a wide margin. Best practice: reach the lake already acclimatized (Arequipa→Colca→Puno→Cusco).

faq.q: Is the boat trip across the lake dangerous?
faq.a: Only if you cut corners on the operator. Titicaca is a huge, cold, high-altitude open lake where afternoon wind picks up fast; insist on a licensed lancha with life vests and prefer guided/operator boats over informal transport. Weather can turn quickly on the altiplano.

faq.q: What is Lalibela?
faq.a: Eleven medieval monolithic churches carved straight down into solid volcanic rock in the late 12th to early 13th century, UNESCO-listed in 1978 and still a living Orthodox worship site. It was conceived as a New Jerusalem so Ethiopian Christians could make pilgrimage at home after Muslim conquests cut off the Holy Land.

faq.q: When do the churches fill with pilgrims?
faq.a: At Genna, Ethiopian Christmas, on 7 January. The dry season runs October to March at roughly 15 to 25C.

faq.q: What are the emergency numbers in Ethiopia?
faq.a: 991 for police, 907 for the Red Cross ambulance, 911 general. An older note circulating as 939 is the fire service, not an ambulance.

name: Les Deux Alpes
line: Glacier skiing on one of Europe's biggest, a two-kilometre

key_facts: France's GLACIER resort (Oisans, Isere, Ecrins edge): Mont-de-Lans glacier - one of Europe's largest skiable; top ~3,600 m (Dome de la Lauze); ~2,000 m in-village vertical (skiresort range 1,280-3,523 m); ~220 km / 96 runs
SUMMER glacier skiing ~mid-June-late August (~110 ha, ~2,800-3,600 m) - a genuine second season (race teams, freestyle camps)
The LA GRAVE link from the Dome de la Lauze - legendary UNPISTED terrain with NO formal avalanche control; 1-2 km walk + glacier travel; GUIDE-REQUIRED (not a casual link)
New JANDRI 3S tri-cable gondola (2024/25) cuts base-to-glacier from ~40 to ~17 min; funicular to ~3,450 m; 214 snow cannons; new pool/ice-rink complex (winter 2025/26)
Rated #1 for apres-ski in Isere - a famously big, young party scene; top-ranked snowpark; short night-skiing pitch
Winter season ~late Nov-early May (29 Nov 2025-3 May 2026); adult day pass ~EUR 66 (6-day/summer flagged); US pass (Ikon) prior-season reported but current UNVERIFIED - do not assert
Access: Grenoble ~71 km/~1h30, Lyon ~2h; bus link to Alpe d'Huez; Meteo-France BERA massif 'Oisans' (verify; distinct from Alpe d'Huez 'Grandes-Rousses')
HELI-SKIING BANNED IN FRANCE - guided touring/glacier off-piste only; NO natural hot springs (nearest thermal Uriage-les-Bains near Grenoble - verify)

safety.emergency: 112 (Europe) / 15 SAMU / 17 police / 18 fire / 114 SMS; mountain rescue via 112 / PGHM (Isere/Oisans)
safety.hospital: Resort clinic; nearest major hospital CHU Grenoble Alpes (~71 km); heli evac SMUR/PGHM
safety.activity_note: High-alpine glacier terrain: off-piste avalanche risk - Meteo-France BERA, 5-level scale, Oisans massif (verify label; distinct from Alpe d'Huez Grandes-Rousses); transceiver/shovel/probe + UIAGM guide; GLACIER/CREVASSE (Mont-de-Lans, Dome de la Lauze ~3,600 m) guided-only off-piste; the LA GRAVE crossing is unpisted with NO avalanche control (1-2 km walk + glacier travel, GUIDE-REQUIRED); NO heli-skiing (banned in France); altitude (AMS on rapid ascent to 3,600 m) + intense glacier glare (cat-3/4); rescue 112/PGHM

name: Lima
line: The world's table, on the Pacific

key_facts: Home to the World's #1 restaurant 2025 (Maido, Nikkei) plus Central (former #1, Best of the Best), Kjolle #9, Merito #26, Mayta #39 - a global top-tier food capital.
Pre-Inca adobe pyramids inside the modern city (Huaca Pucllana, ~200-700 AD, in Miraflores) alongside the UNESCO colonial Centro Historico and the Convento de San Francisco catacombs.

Jorge Chavez (LIM) is South America's newest mega-hub: new $2.4B Fraport/LAP terminal opened June 1, 2025 (3x size, up to 40M pax/yr, 46 gates, 2nd runway); the gateway to Cusco/MP, the Amazon, Titicaca and the south coast.
Cool Pacific-desert climate: warm sunny summer Dec-Apr; grey misty 'garua' winter May-Nov (dry but overcast) - the driest window for Machu Picchu, which drives Lima's derivative winter spike.

Bohemian Barranco (Puente de los Suspiros) and clifftop Miraflores (Malecon, Costa Verde paragliding) anchor the boutique-romance line; genuine global-flag ultra (Belmond, Relais & Chateaux, LHW, JW Marriott).

faq.q: How do I actually get a table at Maido, Central or Kjolle?
faq.a: Book weeks ahead — the tables are the binding constraint, not the hotel. Central, Maido and Kjolle open reservations on a rolling monthly/multi-week basis and sell out, so the culinary itinerary must be built reservation-first; grey winter is fine because the dining is indoors.

faq.q: What can I see in Lima in a day or two?
faq.a: More than you'd expect for a gateway city. Walk to Huaca Pucllana (a ~200–700 AD adobe pyramid in Miraflores), the Convento de San Francisco (founded 1540) catacombs in the UNESCO Centro Histórico, and the Larco Museum's 5,000-year pre-Columbian collection in an 18th-century mansion.

faq.q: Is Lima good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — the base is bohemian Barranco, Lima's most walkable, romantic district, home to the Puente de los Suspiros ("Bridge of Sighs") and to Hotel B, a restored 1914 Belle Époque arts-mansion that is the city's only Relais & Châteaux.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Lima?
faq.a: Urban street crime, not any activity. Stay in Miraflores, Barranco and San Isidro; use only registered radio-taxis, ride-hail apps or hotel transfers — never an unmarked street taxi, the classic express-kidnapping setup (forced ATM withdrawals over 1–3 hours). Use in-bank ATMs and keep valuables out of sight.

faq.q: When is the best time to see blue whales in Loreto?
faq.a: Roughly January–March, strongest early February to about mid-March, because that's when blue whales feed in the bay; gray and humpback come slightly earlier. Tours are 4–6-hour pangas from Loreto Marina or Puerto Escondido — book the short window 3–6 months ahead.

faq.q: What are Loreto's islands like?
faq.a: Five uninhabited islands — Coronado, del Carmen, Danzante, Monserrat and Santa Catalina — shelter the bay with turquoise coves, white-sand beaches and a sea-lion colony, all inside a protected marine park with 40+ snorkel/dive sites. Isla Coronado is the classic day trip.

faq.q: Is Loreto good for a golf-and-spa couples escape?
faq.a: Yes, if you want premier rather than ultra. Villa del Palmar at Danzante Bay has Mexico's only TPC course (Best Golf Course in Mexico 2020) and a 39,000-sq-ft spa on a secluded bay — position it as a premier golf-and-whale escape, not an Aman-tier ultra.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for — is the diving remote?
faq.a: Yes — chamber distance is the gatekeeper. Loreto has local clinics for routine care, but a serious dive bend routes ~350 km south to the La Paz chamber (or Los Cabos), so dive conservatively, keep whale-panga trips to licensed no-chase operators, and observe 18–24 h no-fly before the LTO departure.

faq.q: When is kiteboarding season in Los Barriles?
faq.a: November 1 to the end of March, when the "El Norte" wind blows a reliable 15–30 kt N/NE crosswind, building mid-morning and peaking in the afternoon. The wide, protected sandy bay suits all levels — book instructors and beachfront villas 4–9 months out.

faq.q: When is the fishing best, and what's the big tournament?
faq.a: Offshore peaks May to early November in glass-calm water for marlin, dorado, wahoo and tuna, and the marquee event is the mid-July Dorado Shoot Out — ~140 boats, Baja's largest dorado tournament. Kite and fishing are opposite seasons, so plan for one or the other.

faq.q: What else is there beyond wind and fish?
faq.a: Winter whale-watching (Dec–Apr) offshore, ATV desert-and-beach runs year-round, and the La Paz whale-shark snorkel ~40 minutes north (Oct–Apr). Off the wind season (Apr–Oct) the Sea of Cortez turns calm for swimming, snorkel and SUP.

faq.q: Is kiteboarding here dangerous?
faq.a: It's for the prepared — the core hazard is offshore drift. El Norte's 15–30 kt N/NE wind is side-offshore, so a downed kiter drifts toward open sea; take lessons with a school running rescue-boat cover, use the right kite size and self-rescue skills, and check the daily wind before launch.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Luxor?
faq.a: October to April, with November the sweet spot - comfortable days (~25-30C) and the clearest light for the temples. Summer tops 40C, so tour at dawn and hydrate.

faq.q: How do I do the Nile cruise from Luxor?

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in the Maasai Mara?
faq.a: Dangerous game and remoteness, not the parks. Lions, elephants and buffalo are at close range - stay in the vehicle and follow your guide; at the crossings keep to designated vantage points (3,000+ crocodiles). Ground EMS is limited, so carry AMREF Flying Doctors (~$40 pp/30 days, evac to Nairobi) + travel-medical insurance.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit - migration or big cats?
faq.a: For the Great Migration and Mara River crossings, come Jul-Oct (peak Aug-Sep). For big cats without the migration crush, come Jan-Mar. The long rains (Apr-May) are lush, quiet and cheapest. Book 6-12 months ahead for the Jul-Oct peak.

faq.q: Reserve or a conservancy - what's the difference?
faq.a: The National Reserve has the classic crossings but more vehicles; the surrounding conservancies (community/private land) offer fewer vehicles, walking safaris, off-road and night drives - the more exclusive, often ultra, choice. Many itineraries combine both.

faq.q: How much does a Maasai Mara safari cost?
faq.a: Reserve entry is $200/pp/day (2026 peak); a mid-range 4-day Mara safari runs ~$1,400-2,500/pp including the domestic flight, and a luxury 4-night peak stay $3,450-7,800/pp depending on camp.

faq.q: Do I need a visa or yellow-fever certificate for Kenya?
faq.a: An eTA (Kenya replaced visas with the eTA in 2024 - apply at least 2 weeks ahead; required for all visitors). Yellow fever is compulsory only if you arrive from a YF-risk country (cert valid 10 days post-injection); CDC recommends the vaccine for most.

name: Machu Picchu

key_facts: Machu Picchu citadel sits at 2,430 m; Cusco gateway at ~3,400 m — altitude, not crime, is the headline planning constraint.
Entry is by timed circuit ticket only (no free roaming); daily cap 4,500 standard / 5,600 high season (Jun 19–Nov 2).

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for at Machu Picchu?
faq.a: Altitude, not crime. Cusco sits at ~3,400 m and acute mountain sickness (*soroche*) is the primary health risk — headache, nausea, breathlessness. Acclimatize in the lower Sacred Valley (~2,800 m) before Cusco or any trek, ascend gradually, and rest day one; the citadel itself (2,430 m) is lower, so many feel better there.

faq.q: How hard is the Inca Trail, and do I need a guide?
faq.a: You cannot legally hike the classic trail without a licensed guide, and it is demanding, not casual. Only 500 permits are issued per day (~200 hikers), the trail closes every February, and the Day-2 crux is Dead Woman's Pass at 4,215 m — a ~1,200 m ascent where oxygen is ~60% of sea level. Book 4–7 months ahead for peak.

faq.q: Is the Huayna Picchu climb dangerous?
faq.a: It's exposed but managed — bookable for the sure-footed. Huayna Picchu is a ~2-hour climb capped at 400 permits/day, with big drop-offs, narrow original Inca stairs and cable-assisted sections; it is not for those uneasy with heights. Machu Picchu Mountain is the longer, higher, less-exposed alternative.

faq.q: Is the Belmond Hiram Bingham worth it for a honeymoon?
faq.a: For a marquee honeymoon, yes — it removes the ticket-scramble. The Hiram Bingham bundles citadel entry, bus and guide into a ~1h45m polished-brass rail run, and pairs with the Sanctuary Lodge, the only hotel at the gate (first in at dawn, last out at dusk). Hold both as early as the trek permit.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Machu Picchu?
faq.a: May–October (dry season) is best and June–August is clearest — cloudless mornings — because the wet season (Nov–March) is lusher but rainier and February closes the Inca Trail entirely. The daily citadel cap also rises to 5,600 for the Jun 19–Nov 2 high-season block, so book early.

faq.q: When is gray-whale season in Magdalena Bay?
faq.a: The hard window is roughly mid-January to mid-March, when mothers and calves fill the calving lagoon; whales arrive late Dec–early Jan and linger to April. Mag Bay's grays are famously "friendly," often approaching the pangas — book the tiny whale-camp capacity 6–12 months ahead.

faq.q: Can I snorkel the striped-marlin bait balls?
faq.a: Yes, from about mid-October to December — but it's an advanced open-water activity. You're offshore in current among fast-moving marlin and sea lions driving sardines to the surface, so it's for confident, fit snorkelers and freedivers with specialist operators only.

faq.q: Where do I stay — are there resorts?
faq.a: No resorts — the accurate options are a barrier-island whale camp (glamping, 1–7 nights, ~$650+ for a 1-night all-in) or basic hotels in Puerto San Carlos and López Mateos. The camp is part of the experience: whales from shore, and nothing between you and the lagoon.

faq.q: Is the bait-ball snorkel dangerous?
faq.a: It is not a beginner activity. The sardine run happens offshore in current among fast predators, so go only with specialist operators, follow the guide's positioning rules and never touch the wildlife; if you dive elsewhere in Baja, the nearest chambers are La Paz and Cabo San Lucas with 18–24 h no-fly.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for diving Mahahual?
faq.a: Remote medevac - the load-bearing risk. Mahahual has NO hyperbaric chamber; the nearest DAN-certified chamber is in Cozumel, a multi-hour transit from a Chinchorro site ~25 miles offshore. Dive conservatively, hold no-fly 18-24h, and treat DCS as a logistics problem.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Mahahual and Chinchorro?
faq.a: May-September - the counterintuitive answer: calmest seas, best visibility (~15-30m) and the crocodile season (Jun 1-Sep 30), even though it overlaps the rainy/hurricane months. Winter (Nov-Mar) sees more wind and Chinchorro is often blown out.

faq.q: Can I day-dive Banco Chinchorro, and how?
faq.a: Yes - most Mahahual/Xcalak operators run day-trips for certified divers: a 2-tank ($275) or 3-tank ($325) day with a Cayo Centro stop, an 80-90-minute crossing each way. The operator handles the limited federal permit when you book; May-September has the calmest seas.

faq.q: Can you really swim with wild crocodiles at Chinchorro?
faq.a: Yes - it's the only legally permitted in-water wild-crocodile encounter on Earth, and only XTC Dive Center holds the federal permit. The season is a hard window of June 1 to September 30, capped at 6 people (2 in the water with the handler at a time), flotation device required. Book far ahead.

faq.q: What is the Banco Chinchorro liveaboard experience actually like?
faq.a: It's a stilt-hut expedition, not a cruise ship. Multi-day trips overnight in a palafito on Cayo Centro - a basic 2x2m stilt-deck fishing hut with hammocks and no services - legalized in 2010. It's the closest access to the remote walls and ~200 wrecks; permit-scarce, so book the specialist operator well ahead.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for the Maldives, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places the Maldives at Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution, due to terrorism, with no sub-national carve-out (accessed 2026-08-09). State adds that attacks may occur on remote islands, which can lengthen the response time of authorities - worth weighing on a liveaboard far from Male. The UK FCDO advises against no travel but says terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out and could be indiscriminate; the stricter baseline (State Level 2) sets the posture. Carry DAN membership plus separate dive-accident insurance (liveaboard.com requires divers to independently hold it) and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Master Liveaboards' Maldives FAQ names five operational recompression chambers, with the largest and longest-operating on Bandos Island in North Male Atoll, 15 minutes by speedboat from Male - the closest to a Male departure. Others sit at Kuramathi (North Ari), Kuredu (Lhaviyani, the only chamber in the northern Maldives, with a clinic reporting operators on call 24 hours), Kandima (Dhaalu) and ADK Hospital in Male. Recompression treatment is likely to involve evacuation by private speedboat or seaplane, so confirm the chamber nearest your route and its readiness on your dates with the operator or DAN.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive the Maldives?
faq.a: December-May is the dry northeast-monsoon window - calmer seas, clearer water (15-20 m+), best for channel pelagics. June-November is the southwest monsoon: greener water but the manta and whale-shark season. Water stays 26-29C year-round.

faq.q: When and where do I see mantas and whale sharks?
faq.a: June-October in the southwest monsoon, with Hanifaru Bay in Baa Atoll the signature aggregation site (snorkel-only in the protected core); South Ari Atoll holds whale sharks year-round.

faq.q: Which atolls does a liveaboard week cover?
faq.a: Central-atoll routes work North/South Male, Ari, Vaavu and Baa; southern and specialist routes reach Fuvahmulah (tiger and thresher sharks) and Huvadhoo. Route choice tracks the monsoon - central-atoll clear-water weeks in the northeast season, manta routes in the southwest.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Channel (kandu) dives are current-driven drift dives suited to experienced divers; thila pinnacles and lagoon sites suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards for the multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Maldives liveaboards book?
faq.a: Northeast-season (Dec-Apr) clear-water weeks and manta-season (Jun-Oct) berths on preferred vessels fill earliest; hold roughly 3-9 months out for peak windows, nearer term for shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

name: Mammoth Mountain
line: California's highest mountain, deepest snow, and longest season

key_facts: Mammoth = Alterra / Ikon (Alterra HQ Denver); CALIFORNIA'S HIGHEST ski resort (summit 11,053 ft, base 7,953 ft, ~3,100 ft vertical; town ~7,880 ft); a VOLCANIC lava-dome complex on the Long Valley Caldera
3,500+ acres, 175-178 trails (15% beg / 48% int / 37% adv), 25 lifts (~59,000/hr); ~400 in snow; no night skiing
ONE OF THE LONGEST SEASONS IN THE US: Nov-May typical, often into June, sometimes July - regularly the last major US resort open; distinctive long-spring demand window
Alterra also owns June Mountain (~1,500 ac, 41 trails, family-oriented) ~20+ mi N near June Lake

GENUINE natural hot springs in the Eastern Sierra (a real, rare ski-trip amenity): Benton Hot Springs confirmed (~135F source); Long Valley/Crowley springs widely known - Wellness is LIVE via the natural springs, NOT a hotel-spa claim
US-TRAFFIC CANDOR: among CA's biggest/most-visited but no per-resort count published - consensus only
Long haul: LA ~5 hr / Reno ~3 hr via US-395; Mammoth Yosemite Airport (MMH) ~7 mi E seasonal winter flights (weather-unreliable); TIOGA PASS (SR-120) CLOSED in winter -> Bay Area detour
NO on-site cat/heli (lift-served; regional guided touring only); VOLCANIC CO2 hazard near Horseshoe Lake; Hot Creek soaking PROHIBITED (dangerous geothermal); Ikon/lift prices dynamic

safety.hospital: Mammoth Hospital, Mammoth Lakes - small critical-access hospital, 24/7 ER (site 403'd - verify); larger Northern Inyo Hospital in Bishop (~40 mi S)
safety.activity_note: ALTITUDE (base ~7,953 ft GENUINELY HIGH, summit ~11,053 ft; SoCal drive market arrives sea-level - hydrate, ease alcohol, descend if AMS worsens); VOLCANIC CO2 (Horseshoe Lake ~170-ac tree-kill zone can hold lethal CO2 in depressions/snow-wells/cabins - avoid low pockets, heed signage); AVALANCHE backcountry - Eastern Sierra Avalanche Center (ESAC, esavalanche.org, 'eastside-region' - VERIFY named sub-zones); beacon/probe/shovel + guide, never duck ropes; tree-wells; US-395 winter driving + Caltrans chains + TIOGA PASS (SR-120) closed all winter; HOT CREEK soaking PROHIBITED (scalding/fluctuating geothermal - use only established safe springs)

name: Manuel Antonio
line: Sloths, monkeys and Pacific cliffs

key_facts: Manuel Antonio NP is open Wed–Mon 07:00–16:00, CLOSED every Tuesday; adult entry US$18, child (2–12) US$5, under-2 free; advance online ticket + passport number required.

One of few places to see all of Costa Rica's iconic wildlife at a beach: 2- & 3-toed sloths, white-faced capuchins (90%+ of visits), endangered Central American squirrel monkeys, howlers, coatis, toucans.
Two park beaches: crescent Playa Manuel Antonio (calm, turquoise — best/safest swim) and longer, choppier Playa Espadilla Sur.
Access: ~2.5–3 hr / ~168 km drive from San José (SJO), OR ~25-min domestic flight to Quepos–Manuel Antonio (XQP) on Sansa / Costa Rica Green Airways + 15 km / 25-min transfer.
Cliffside-resort belt (Arenas del Mar, Makanda, Gaia, Tulemar) makes it a top romance/honeymoon hub; hillside villas make it a strong family/multi-gen hub.

safety.hospital: Hospital Metropolitano Quepos (private, 24-hr, marina) + public Max Terán Valls Hospital; serious cases to San José major hospitals (~2.5–3 hr) with air evac available
safety.advisory_note: US Level 2 Exercise Increased Caution (reissued 2026-04-02); clean L2, no L4 zone near Manuel Antonio/Quepos; standard caution — petty crime, don't display wealth, avoid poorly lit beaches at night, enroll in STEP
safety.air_access_verified: SJO gateway; XQP (Quepos–Manuel Antonio) ~25-min domestic flight on Sansa / Costa Rica Green Airways, or ~2.5–3 hr drive from SJO
safety.riptide: HARD FLAG — rip currents are the leading cause of tourist drowning in Costa Rica (>80% of drownings); most beaches unguarded. Swim only at guarded/flagged beaches (park cove safest), heed red flags, never swim alone; if caught, swim parallel to shore.
safety.wildlife: Bold habituated monkeys/raccoons/coatis raid food — no feeding, seal food, don't leave bags unattended
safety.dengue: Year-round mosquito-borne risk (higher green season May–Nov); no widely available traveler vaccine — DEET/picaridin, cover at dawn/dusk, screened/AC rooms
safety.water: Tap water in San José & major tourist areas (incl. Manuel Antonio/Quepos) treated and generally safe; sensitive stomachs / remote lodges use bottled/filtered

faq.q: Is Manuel Antonio National Park open on Tuesday?
faq.a: No — the park is closed every Tuesday, year-round including holidays. It is open Wednesday–Monday 07:00–16:00; adult entry is $18, children 2–12 $5, under-2 free, and advance online ticket purchase with your passport number is required — route the park visit Wed–Mon.

faq.q: Can you see whales near Manuel Antonio?
faq.a: Yes — nearby Marino Ballena / Uvita has two humpback seasons. Southern-Hemisphere humpbacks run Jul–Oct/Nov (peak Aug–Sep) and Northern-Hemisphere humpbacks Dec–Mar/Apr (peak Jan–Feb), a rare draw spanning both the green and dry seasons, ~45–60 min south by guided boat tour.

faq.q: Is Manuel Antonio good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — it's one of Costa Rica's premier romance hubs. The cliffside-resort belt above the beach, led by adults-only Makanda by the Sea ~100 m above the ocean, defines the honeymoon identity, while Arenas del Mar is the only true beachfront luxury resort with two private beaches.

faq.q: Can you really see sloths and monkeys at the beach?
faq.a: Yes — it's one of very few places anywhere you reliably can. Two- and three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchins (on 90%+ of visits), the endangered Central American squirrel monkey, howlers, coatis and toucans all live inside a compact, walkable national park where the rainforest meets the sand.

faq.q: What's the biggest safety risk in Manuel Antonio?
faq.a: Pacific rip currents — the leading cause of tourist drowning in Costa Rica (over 80% of drownings), on mostly unguarded beaches. Swim only at guarded/flagged beaches (the calm park cove of Playa Manuel Antonio is safest), heed red flags, never swim alone, and if caught, swim parallel to shore.

faq.q: Are the monkeys a problem in the park?
faq.a: They can be — capuchins, raccoons and coatis are bold and habituated and will raid open bags and grab food. Don't feed wildlife, keep food sealed and bags zipped, and don't leave belongings unattended on the beach.

faq.q: Can I play golf in Marrakech?

name: Mayrhofen
line: Austria's steepest piste, a world-class freestyle park, 476 km

key_facts: Two home mountains: Penken (main; Harakiri + Penken Park freestyle) + Ahorn (sunny beginner side; Ahornbahn = Austria's largest cable car, 160-pax)
Local Mayrhofen area ~142 km / ~60 lifts (blue ~40/red ~66/black ~33); top ~2,500 m; village ~630 m; season ~late Nov-late April
The Harakiri = Austria's steepest groomed piste (widely reported ~78% / ~38 deg - exact figure to verify; not asserted)
Penken Park = one of Austria's best freestyle snowparks
Zillertal Superskipass = ~476.3 km / 187 lifts across 7 areas on one ticket (car-free via the Zillertalbahn)
Hintertux Glacier (~20 km up the Tuxertal) = one of only 2 year-round/365-day ski resorts on earth (with Zermatt); 64 km winter, to 3,250 m, longest run ~12 km
Snowbombing = the original mountain music festival, based in Mayrhofen since 2005, each spring (2027 = 5-10 April)
Big apres reputation (Ice Bar, Niki's Schirmbar among the names - venues to verify)
Reached via Jenbach + the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn; Innsbruck ~1 hr; Munich/Salzburg airports
No confirmed Ikon/Epic affiliation (own product = Zillertal Superskipass)
Strong 4/5-star hotel base with spas (e.g. Elisabethhotel - ratings to verify)
Heli-skiing NOT available (Austria permits it only at Vorarlberg/Lech-Zurs sites)
Avalanche = Lawinenwarndienst Tirol via Euregio lawinen.report, EAWS 5-level - NOT SLF/Meteo
Nearest hospital = Bezirkskrankenhaus Schwaz (~35 km; verify)
A rare four-season mountain: winter area + freestyle park + spring festival + year-round Hintertux glacier

safety.emergency: 112 EU general / 140 Bergrettung alpine rescue / 144 ambulance / 133 police / 122 fire
safety.hospital: Bezirkskrankenhaus Schwaz (~35 km down-valley; verify); local practice for day cases; 140 Bergrettung / helicopter alpine evac
safety.activity_note: Steeps (Harakiri) + freestyle park + off-piste + Hintertux glacier: park-injury discipline (helmet/back protection, feature build-up) + avalanche (Lawinenwarndienst Tirol via lawinen.report, EAWS 5-level; transceiver/shovel/probe + guide off-piste) + crevasse on glacier (roped-and-guided); heli NOT available (Austria = Vorarlberg only); rescue 140 Bergrettung

faq.q: Can I book a stay in Mazamitla through TravelWell?
faq.a: No — it is content-only, recommended only as a licensed day/weekend trip from the Guadalajara carve-out. Jalisco is US State Dept Level 3 (May 29, 2026) and Mazamitla is not one of the four named carve-outs; notably, though, the advisory names Mazamitla as an exception to the Highway 110 restriction and permits access "via Highway 405 only." book_enabled=FALSE.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: The ~2-hour mountain road transfer, not the town's street crime (which is low — a domestic family town). The drive from Guadalajara leaves the GDL safe zone, even on the advisory-approved Highway 405, which is the hold reason; use licensed daytime transport only, and note the nearest full trauma hospital is ~2 hr back in Guadalajara.

faq.q: What is there to do at El Salto waterfall?
faq.a: Hike to it. The ~35 m El Salto falls in Los Cazos are reached by a ~45-minute forest trail (or a horse, ~M$250) to a wooden overlook, entry ~US$1, with the fullest flow October–December after the rains. Sturdy footwear, and turn back in weather.

faq.q: Is Mazamitla good for a family weekend?
faq.a: Yes — it is the classic Guadalajara family escape. The product is a wooden chalet cabaña with a full kitchen and fireplace (Cabañas Monteverde delivers firewood daily) in a cool ~15°C pine-oak Pueblo Mágico at 2,200 m; cabañas sell out for Semana Santa, summer and Christmas, so book weeks to months ahead.

faq.q: What adventure activities are on offer?
faq.a: Zip, ride and cross bridges. Green Forest Tours runs a 3-hour zipline and a 2-hour six-hanging-bridge walk, plus ATV, horseback and mountain-biking through the forest and Los Cazos. Use licensed operators with helmet/harness checks — evac to Guadalajara is ~2 hr, so injuries carry a distance penalty.

faq.q: Is Medellín a good place for a couples trip or honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — for couples arriving together. El Poblado luxury apartments, rooftop-pool hotels and coffee-finca escapes are genuinely romantic. The plain caveat: the US Embassy links 8 suspicious US-citizen deaths in Medellín (Nov–Dec 2023) to dating-app-lured druggings, so the safe lane is partners who arrive together, not app meet-ups.

faq.q: What is Comuna 13 and is it worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes — Comuna 13 is Medellín's most-visited site and the emblem of its turnaround. Outdoor public escalators installed in 2011 cut a 35-minute climb to 6 minutes; today the hillside barrio is a canvas of community murals, told on a guided walking tour (~$20–30). Go guided, daytime, as a group.

faq.q: How do you visit Guatapé and El Peñol rock from Medellín?
faq.a: Guatapé sits about 2 hours east, usually as a full-day trip. The headline is climbing El Peñol (Piedra del Peñol) via 740 steps — most reach the top in 15–25 minutes — over a reservoir dotted with islands, then wandering the brightly painted zócalo streets. Book a day-trip operator or DMC.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Medellín?
faq.a: The signature Medellín danger is dating-app drugging-and-robbery, not the headlines. The US Embassy is aware of 8 suspicious US-citizen deaths (Nov 1–Dec 31, 2023) involving scopolamine ("burundanga") — odorless, memory-erasing and lethal in large doses. Don't meet app strangers alone, never leave a drink unattended, and meet only in public.

faq.q: Is climbing El Peñol's 740 steps dangerous?
faq.a: It's a steep but manageable self-guided climb — 740 steps, 15–25 minutes for most — though not for those with cardiac or mobility limits. Pace it, hydrate, and mind your footing on the descent. Paragliding over the Aburrá Valley, by contrast, should be flown only with certified, insured, safety-vetted operators.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Cambodia?
faq.a: Landmines/UXO - the safety-spine item, avalanche-level weight. Contamination persists in provinces including Siem Reap; stay strictly on marked paths and cleared temple routes, never wander into fields or unmarked ground. Petty bag-snatch is the secondary caution.

faq.q: Are the closed Thai borders a problem for a Mekong cruise?
faq.a: No. All Cambodia-Thailand land crossings are closed (2026), but the Mekong cruise enters Cambodia by river from Vietnam at Tan Chau, and Siem Reap/Phnom Penh connect by flight - so cruise itineraries are unaffected. It only matters for overland Thailand-Cambodia travel.

faq.q: When is the best time to cruise the Cambodian Mekong?
faq.a: Roughly November-April (dry, cooler); the Tonle Sap is highest and most navigable after the wet season (Oct-Dec), when the lake and its floating villages are fullest.

faq.q: Which lines cruise the Cambodian Mekong?
faq.a: Confirmed: Aqua Expeditions (Aqua Mekong), Pandaw, Scenic, Uniworld, CroisiEurope and Viking - most on Vietnam-Cambodia itineraries, Siem Reap to Phnom Penh via the Tonle Sap and Kampong Cham.

faq.q: Is Angkor Wat worth building the trip around?
faq.a: Yes - Angkor is the largest religious monument on earth and the reason most cruises terminate at Siem Reap; pair the temples with the Tonle Sap floating villages and a Phnom Penh Khmer-Rouge history day for the full Cambodian arc.

faq.a: Not crime - heat, traffic and the water: the delta is hot and humid year-round, Ho Chi Minh City traffic is dense, and canal sampans are small craft (follow crew, wear the life vest). Standard SE-Asia food-and-water hygiene applies.

faq.q: Is the Vietnam-Cambodia border crossing on a Mekong cruise a problem?
faq.a: No - the cruise river crossing at Tan Chau is open and routinely used by the ships. (Separately, some Cambodia-Thailand land borders are closed - that affects the Cambodia leg, not this Vietnamese one.)

faq.q: When is the best time to cruise the Vietnamese Mekong?
faq.a: Roughly November-April, the drier cooler window, because the May-October wet season brings heavy afternoon rain and higher water - though the delta cruises year-round and high water opens more canals.

faq.q: Which lines cruise the Vietnamese Mekong?
faq.a: Confirmed from Ho Chi Minh City: Viking, Aqua Expeditions, Uniworld, Scenic and Mekong Navigator - most on Vietnam-Cambodia itineraries linking the delta to Phnom Penh and Siem Reap.

faq.q: What do you actually see in the Mekong Delta?
faq.a: River life: the Cai Be floating market, Sa Dec's colonial streets and flower gardens, Ben Tre's coconut canals by sampan, cooking classes with delta chefs, and - near the start - the Cu Chi tunnels of the Vietnam War.

faq.q: Is the Mekong Delta good for a river-cruise honeymoon or for older travellers?
faq.a: Yes to both - small-ship 5-star cruising (Aqua Mekong ~40 guests) suits a quiet honeymoon, and the gentle all-in format with step-light excursions and HCMC as an easy gateway fits the river-cruise senior demographic.

faq.q: Why is Mendoza the world's Malbec capital?
faq.a: Because the concentration is unmatched: Argentina holds roughly 75% of the world's Malbec vines, and about 75% of Argentina's vineyards lie in Mendoza — making it the single most important place on the planet for the grape and the global epicenter of Malbec.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Mendoza?
faq.a: Late February through April — harvest and the Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia (2026 central acts Mar 6–10) — is the most atmospheric window. Spring (Oct–Nov) is the value-and-balance alternative, with rates running ~15–25% below harvest peaks; either way, book icon wineries and lodges 3–4 months ahead of the Feb–April peak.

faq.q: Which honeymoon wine-lodge should we book?
faq.a: The two ultra beds are Awasi Mendoza (Relais & Châteaux, Luján de Cuyo, 18 adobe rooms/villas on a ~60-acre private vineyard) and The Vines Resort & Spa (Valle de Uco, 21 private villas across 1,500 acres with vine-side dining). Both commission best through luxury consortia (Virtuoso/Fora), typically ~10%+ plus amenities.

faq.q: Can you see Aconcagua on a day trip from Mendoza?
faq.a: Yes. Route 7 climbs the Alta Montaña corridor past Potrerillos (1,350 m), Uspallata (1,900 m), and Puente del Inca (2,720 m) to the Aconcagua Provincial Park viewpoint of the 6,961 m peak, the highest in the Western Hemisphere. The day-trip tops out ~2,700 m (mild breathlessness possible); Aconcagua summit mountaineering is a separate, expedition-grade activity requiring permits and licensed guides.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Mendoza?
faq.a: Drink-driving. Wine touring plus self-drive is the single most important avoidable risk, so the standard doctrine is always a designated driver or a guided wine tour with transport — never self-drive between tastings, and ride sober on the Maipú bike-and-wine route.

faq.q: Is Mendoza River rafting dangerous?
faq.a: Guided, it is a managed risk. Rafting at Potrerillos runs Class II–III, up to Class IV in high summer flow, with certified rescue guides, kayak safety support, and full neoprene/helmet/PFD standard — book certified operators only, and never run the river unguided.

faq.q: Why is Mérida the hacienda-wedding capital, and how far ahead do I book?
faq.a: Because the restored henequen haciendas — chapel ruins, walled gardens, private cenotes — are a wedding backdrop found nowhere else, backed by a mature, English-fluent planner ecosystem. Book the date and core vendors 6–12 months out (advisors say 10–12 for high season), the longest-lead, highest-margin flow in the destination.

faq.q: What are the best day-trips from Mérida?
faq.a: Cenotes and flamingos, mostly within ~1.5 hr. The closest swimmable cenote and ruin is Dzibilchaltún (~20 min); the Cuzamá/Homún cenote country is reached by horse-drawn rail-cart (~1 hr); Celestún's flamingo biosphere is ~1.5 hr west; and Uxmal + the Ruta Puuc lie ~1.5 hr south. Chichén Itzá is ~1.5 hr east, best done at dawn.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Mérida?
faq.a: December through April is the dry-cool peak (highs ~84°F, lows ~64°F), but the smartest window is the late-October Hanal Pixán opening (Oct 25–Nov 2), when the heat breaks and hurricane season ends — the Festival de las Ánimas fills the streets with altars and the candlelit Paseo de las Ánimas, mostly free to attend. November and late April are softer-rate shoulders.

faq.q: What should I eat in Mérida?
faq.a: Yucatecan food, which stands apart from central-Mexican cooking. The signature is cochinita pibil — pork marinated in achiote and bitter orange, wrapped in banana leaves and slow-roasted in an underground pit — best at the 1887 Mercado Lucas de Gálvez (~2,000 stalls), alongside sopa de lima, papadzules, salbutes and panuchos.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Mérida?
faq.a: Heat, not crime. May–September is hot-humid and April–June can exceed 100°F (38°C), so run daytime ruin and cenote-country outings on an extreme-heat protocol: dawn starts, hat and high SPF, electrolytes, a midday shade break, and no midday Chichén or Uxmal in summer. Drink bottled water only, and use repellent — dengue is present and chikungunya rose in 2025–26 (no malaria in the corridor).

faq.q: When is the best time to visit the Moroccan desert?
faq.a: October to April - warm days and crisp, starry nights. June to August is dangerously hot (40C+), so avoid high summer.

faq.q: How do I get to Merzouga?
faq.a: The classic overland from Marrakech (3-6 days) - over the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Ait Benhaddou, through the Dades and Todra gorges, then a camel trek into the dunes to your camp. Fez is the shorter alternative bookend.

faq.q: What are the luxury desert camps like?
faq.a: En-suite dome tents with real beds and bathrooms, hosted dining, camel treks and stargazing - the Sahara without roughing it. Rates run about EUR290-460/night at Erg Chebbi and around GBP320 at Erg Chigaga's Nubia camp.

faq.q: Will the altitude affect me?
faq.a: It can for the first day or two. The city sits at **~2,240 m (7,349 ft)** — roughly 25% less oxygen than sea level — and most travelers need **24–72 hours** to acclimate; mild headache, fatigue and breathlessness are common on arrival from sea level and pass with rest, hydration and easing off alcohol on day one. Fitness and age do not predict susceptibility.

faq.q: Is Mexico City good for a romantic city break?
faq.a: Strongly — it's the one live-launch SI that genuinely fits an inland capital. The romance lane is Polanco/Reforma luxe: the St. Regis atop the **31-story Torre Libertad**, the Sofitel's **38th-floor pool**, rooftop dining, and the March–April jacaranda bloom that turns Roma-Condesa purple.

faq.q: What are the must-see culture sites, and is Teotihuacán worth it?
faq.a: Yes — the heritage circuit runs from the Museo Nacional de Antropología (the Aztec Sun Stone) and Templo Mayor beneath the Zócalo out to Teotihuacán, ~50 km northeast, best at dawn by private balloon (**$150–$300 USD**). It's the single greatest day-trip from the city.

faq.q: Do I need reservations for Pujol and the top restaurants?
faq.a: Yes — book weeks ahead. Pujol (top-5 on Latin America's 50 Best) and Quintonil sell their tasting menus out well in advance, and Casa Luis Barragán tickets release Tuesdays at noon CDMX time and sell out within minutes. Lock the marquee tables the moment the trip is confirmed.

faq.q: Where's the best nightlife and cocktail scene?
faq.a: Roma-Condesa. Licorería Limantour was named **Best Bar in North America in 2022 and 2023**, and the surrounding streets hold the city's densest cluster of cocktail bars, mezcalerías and traditional pulquerías — best done as a guided crawl.

faq.q: When is Día de Muertos, and can I see the parade?
faq.a: Oct 31–Nov 2, with the Grand Parade on ~Nov 1 running **~6 km** from Chapultepec down Reforma to the Zócalo — the biggest live-culture moment of the CDMX year. Parade-corridor hotels (Centro/Reforma) tighten sharply through October, so book weeks out.

name: Monteverde
line: The original cloud forest

key_facts: Birthplace of the commercial canopy zipline; Selvatura runs 13 ziplines incl. a 1 km line, 15 platforms, Tarzan swing, and 8 hanging bridges (51-170 m long, 12-60 m high).
Cloud forest protects 400+ bird species (resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird), 2,500+ plants incl. 500+ orchids, 100+ mammals.
Three reserves: Monteverde Cloud Forest ($25, 7AM-4PM), Santa Elena (quieter, great quetzals), Curi-Cancha (least crowded, top birding).
Resplendent quetzal breeds Feb-Jun (peak Mar-Apr), best viewed 6-9 AM on wild-avocado trees.
Highland ~1,400 m; ~3-4 hr from SJO with a rough, partly-unpaved final mountain road; dengue risk low at elevation.

faq.q: Which is the best zipline in Monteverde?
faq.a: It depends on your appetite. Selvatura's flagship runs 13 ziplines including a 1 km line, 15 platforms, a Tarzan swing and 8 hanging bridges; 100% Aventura is the adrenaline pick with 11 ziplines including two Superman lines; Sky Adventures is the family-friendly tram-up, zip-down option.

faq.q: When is quetzal season in Monteverde?
faq.a: Peak sightings run February–June (breeding), with March–April the sweet spot. Best hours are 6–9 AM, when males feed on wild avocado; a guided dawn quetzal walk (~$40–80, 2–3 hrs) is among Costa Rica's best-value wildlife experiences.

faq.q: Is Monteverde good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — it's a genuine eco-romance hub, not a beach substitute. Adults-only Hidden Canopy Treehouses are the honeymoon centerpiece, and Hotel Belmar offers Forest Superior rooms with a jacuzzi and private terrace for a mist-and-forest soak; both run boutique-luxe, not palace-scale.

faq.q: Is ziplining in Monteverde dangerous?
faq.a: It's high-consequence if gear or technique fails, so ride only with certified operators. Confirm harness and dual-brake systems, helmet and stated weight limits before booking with Selvatura, Sky Adventures or 100% Aventura — high-speed lines and Superman/Tarzan configurations raise the stakes.

faq.q: How hard is the drive to Monteverde?
faq.a: It's a real mountain climb. Monteverde sits at ~1,400 m, roughly 3–4 hours from Juan Santamaría (SJO), with the final stretch a rough, partly-unpaved and fog-prone road — drive in daylight, 4WD recommended, allow extra time.

faq.q: Where can I go on safari instead, right now?
faq.a: Kenya (Maasai Mara / Amboseli, US L2, bookable) or Tanzania (Serengeti / Ngorongoro, US L3, bookable) for the classic Big-game plains - or Akagera, Rwanda (US L3, a Big-Five comeback ~2h from Kigali) for the nearest live savanna. We route all Uganda safari demand there.

faq.q: Will this clear - should I wait for Murchison?
faq.a: Possibly - this is a health-driven, dynamic advisory (an outbreak, not conflict), so it can be lifted when the outbreak is contained. We re-verify Uganda's status every publish cycle and will flip the park to bookable the moment it drops below Level 4. For a firm 2026 safari, book Kenya, Tanzania or Akagera now.

faq.q: What would Murchison offer when it reopens?
faq.a: Uganda's largest park - the world's most powerful waterfall (the Nile through a 7-m gorge), four of the Big Five plus Nubian giraffe, the Nile boat safari to the falls' base, delta shoebill cruises and a top-of-falls hike. All held until the advisory lifts.

faq.q: Is there rhino - is it a Big Five park?
faq.a: Four of the five: lion, elephant, buffalo and leopard live in the park - no rhino in Murchison itself. Rhino are seen at the separate Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary on the drive up from Kampala (also held while Uganda is L4).

faq.q: What are the non-Ebola health requirements for Uganda?
faq.a: Yellow fever is mandatory for entry (all travelers >=1 yr, checked at Entebbe, vaccinate >=10 days before); malaria prophylaxis is essential (all regions); carry AMREF Flying Doctors + insurance. All moot while the L4 hold stands.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for Muscat, and can I book it through TravelWell?
faq.a: Oman is at U.S. State Department Level 3 - Reconsider Travel, and Muscat cannot be booked through TravelWell right now. The armed conflict that began 28 February 2026 (U.S./Israeli strikes on Iran; Iranian retaliatory strikes on all six GCC states; the Strait of Hormuz - which Oman borders - closed to commercial shipping; a State 'depart now' order on 2 March 2026) is ongoing as of 2026-08-10. TravelWell books Level 3 only through a consent gate that is not built, so no Gulf destination is bookable regardless of level. Re-verify the level and flight picture before any travel.

name: Ngorongoro Crater
line: The world's largest caldera

key_facts: World's largest intact volcanic caldera (UNESCO 1979) - 600-m walls, 2-3 M years old; ~25,000 large mammals at Africa's highest predator density
The best Big-Five-in-one-day in Africa (lion, elephant, buffalo, leopard, resident black rhino <30); ideal first safari
Olduvai Gorge (cradle of mankind - Homo habilis, ~3.6 M-year fossils) within the Conservation Area; Maasai coexist and graze the highlands
Game dense YEAR-ROUND (animals stay in the crater); dry Jun-Oct clearest, Jan-Feb greener/quieter, Apr-May cheapest; usually 1 crater day in a Northern-Circuit loop
US L3 Reconsider Travel (terrorism = Mtwara far south, NOT the circuit; LGBTQ+ flagged); NCAA fees pass-through ($70.80/adult + $295/vehicle descent + VAT); sold via safari DMCs IATAN-not-CLIA
TZS but USD is the safari currency; eVisa; malaria prophylaxis advised (lower at rim); Seneto descent ~600m steep; AMREF Flying Doctors for evac

safety.hospital: Remote - AMREF Flying Doctors (~$40 pp/30d) + travel-medical insurance; nearest referral Arusha

safety.activity_note: L3 DISCLOSE + CONSENT (terrorism = Mtwara far south, NOT the circuit; LGBTQ+ targeting flagged). Dangerous game at close range on the floor - stay in the vehicle, follow the guide. Seneto descent ~600m steep/narrow (dry conditions, 4x4). Rim altitude ~2,200-2,300m mild effects. Remote - carry AMREF evac + insurance

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for at Ngorongoro?
faq.a: Dangerous game and the descent, not crime. Big game is at close range on the crater floor - stay in the vehicle and follow your guide; the one-way Seneto descent drops ~600m on a steep narrow road (best in dry conditions). Carry AMREF Flying Doctors evac + travel-medical insurance for the remoteness.

faq.q: Should LGBTQ+ travelers be aware of anything in Tanzania?
faq.a: Yes, plainly - Tanzanian law criminalizes same-sex relations and the US advisory flags targeting of LGBTQ+ travelers; a real consideration we'll discuss candidly before booking.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Ngorongoro Crater?
faq.a: Game is dense year-round (the animals don't leave the crater), so it's about crowds: dry Jun-Oct is best-viewing but busiest; Jan-Feb is green, quieter and pairs with the Serengeti calving; Apr-May is cheapest.

faq.q: Is Ngorongoro worth it and how does it fit a trip?
faq.a: Yes - unmatched density and a true Big-Five day in one compact location, ideal for first-time safari-goers. It's usually one crater day within a Northern-Circuit loop (Serengeti + Tarangire/Manyara).

faq.q: What does it cost to enter Ngorongoro?
faq.a: The NCAA fees are significant and pass-through: ~$70.80/adult conservation entry + a $295/vehicle crater-descent fee (plus VAT), bundled into your DMC package; the safari land (lodge + game drive) is where advisor commission sits.

Terrain: 50.8 km pistes (22.4 easy / 18.2 intermediate / 10.2 difficult), 32 lifts, base 255 m to 1,188 m, vertical 933 m

Backcountry gate system pioneered in Japan (first gates 1999); 11 gates today; strict Niseko Rules; out-of-bounds rescue charged min JPY 100,000

faq.q: Which Nicoya beach is best for families and calm swimming?
faq.a: Sámara is the pick. Its long horseshoe bay is calm and reef-protected, making it the peninsula's safest swim and best family beach for kayaking, snorkeling and SUP — a gentler alternative to the surf breaks at Guiones and Santa Teresa.

faq.q: Is Nosara good for beginner surfers?
faq.a: Yes — Playa Guiones is a forgiving beach break with surf schools and whitewater, and Nosara sees 300+ surfable days a year, so beginners can learn nearly any day. Advanced surfers should head to the heavier point/reef swell at Santa Teresa / Mal País instead.

faq.q: When is the Ostional turtle arribada?
faq.a: Year-round, but it peaks Jul–Nov and is biggest Sep–Oct, when up to ~500,000 olive-ridleys come ashore. Events cluster on the ~28-day lunar cycle — around the last-quarter moon and the dark nights just before the new moon — and access is guided-only.

faq.q: Is Nosara or Santa Teresa better for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Both work — pick your mood. Nosara pairs wellness-retreat honeymoons with its lived-in yoga scene; Santa Teresa / Mal País is the remote boho-luxury surf-and-sunset coast, with elite jungle-beach villas and barefoot-ultra properties like Latitude 10 for total privacy.

faq.q: What is the Nicoya Blue Zone?
faq.a: It's Costa Rica's official Blue Zone — one of only five global longevity zones. A 2013 study found the region had roughly 3–4× the global proportion of centenarians, and Nosara's yoga culture is local and lived-in, not imported for tourists.

faq.q: What's the #1 safety risk on this coast?
faq.a: Rip currents. The State Department explicitly warns that dozens of U.S. citizens die yearly in Costa Rica surf, and both Guiones and Santa Teresa have strong riptides — swim only in designated/guarded areas and heed local surf-instructor guidance.

faq.q: Can anyone watch the Ostional arribada?
faq.a: No — access is guided-only. Ostional is a community-managed refuge where guided access is mandatory, with no lights or flash and no touching, respecting nesting-window rules; unguided night beach access is both a wildlife-harm and personal-safety issue.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for at Nyerere?
faq.a: Not the northern Rufiji sector - the advisory's concerns are the far-southern reaches toward the Mozambique border (terrorism, kept out of itineraries) and city petty crime, plus a flagged LGBTQ+ targeting concern travelers should weigh (Tanzanian law criminalizes same-sex relations). Practically: it's a low-elevation river park, so malaria prophylaxis is essential, and keep back from hippos and crocs on the boat.

faq.q: What makes Nyerere different from a northern-circuit safari?
faq.a: The water. Alongside game drives and walking safaris, Nyerere's signature is the Rufiji River boat safari - drifting past hippo pods, big crocodiles and extraordinary birdlife - an experience you can't have in the Serengeti or Ngorongoro. Add one of Africa's best wild-dog populations and near-empty wilderness, and it's the standout of the southern circuit.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Nyerere?
faq.a: The dry season, Jun-Oct, when game concentrates on the Rufiji and its lakes; the green season (Nov-Mar) is lush and excellent for birding, while the long rains (Apr-May) close some camps and soften the roads.

faq.q: How do I get to Nyerere, and how long should I stay?
faq.a: By short fly-in from Dar (~45 min) or a 4-6-hour road transfer; give it 3-4 nights to combine boat safaris, game drives and a walking safari - ideally paired with Ruaha for a full southern-circuit week.

faq.q: Do I need a visa or yellow-fever certificate for Tanzania?
faq.a: eVisa required - apply on the official portal before departure. Yellow fever is not required direct from the US/Europe, but is mandatory if you transit >12 h through a risk country like Kenya.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for at Nyungwe?
faq.a: The trek and the health advisory - not crime. Chimp trekking is a strenuous 2-6-hour hike over steep, slippery montane slopes (good boots + fitness), and the canopy walkway sways 70 m up (a head-for-heights helps). Malaria is present (prophylaxis + DEET, lower at altitude), and it's remote - carry AMREF Flying Doctors + insurance.

faq.q: How much is chimp trekking, and how does it compare to gorillas?
faq.a: The chimp permit is $250 (vs Rwanda's $1,500 gorilla permit) - a more affordable, more active primate trek: faster-moving chimps, a 2-6-hour hike, a one-hour encounter (7-8 m distance, a face mask, an armed ranger). It pairs beautifully with the gorillas of Volcanoes.

faq.q: What else is there besides chimps at Nyungwe?
faq.a: Plenty: the canopy walk ($60), huge colobus troops (up to 400), the Isumo waterfall hike ($15), world-class birding (29 Albertine-Rift endemics), and tea plantations on the forest edge - Nyungwe rewards a 2-3-day stay.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Nyungwe?
faq.a: For hiking, the canopy walk and general primates, come in the drier Jun-Sep and Dec-Feb (firmer trails); for chimp trekking, the wetter Oct-May can be better (abundant fruit keeps chimps lower and closer).

faq.q: Do I need a visa or yellow-fever certificate for Rwanda?
faq.a: Visa on arrival $30 (or online via Irembo); passport valid 6 months. Yellow fever is required only if arriving from a YF-endemic country (not direct from the US).

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Terrain and high-proof spirits, not crime. The city is a mild **~1,555 m** (light first-day breathlessness at most); the genuine hazards are Hierve el Agua's cliff-edge footing above a canyon and the mezcal route — high-proof tastings plus rural highway driving mean you take a driver or DMC, never self-drive after tasting.

faq.q: When is Día de Muertos, and how far ahead do I book?
faq.a: Oct 31–Nov 2, and it's the longest lead time in the inland catalog: book **4–8 months ahead** (5–6 months / May–June is the sweet spot). Walkable-Centro rooms are ~95% booked by early September and rates run **2–3× normal** ($150–250 USD/night).

faq.q: Is Oaxaca really a top food destination?
faq.a: Yes — it's widely regarded as one of the world's great food capitals. The "seven moles," market-to-table cooking schools (Casa Crespo), and the mezcal terroir of Santiago Matatlán (~45 minutes southeast, the World Capital of Mezcal) are destination-defining reasons to go.

faq.q: Is Hierve el Agua worth it — and will it be open?
faq.a: Worth it, but verify first. The petrified mineral "waterfalls" and clifftop spring-fed pools sit 70 km east near Mitla, but the site sees **periodic community-dispute closures clustering June–October** — always confirm it's open the week before, and keep a Mitla + Tlacolula fallback ready.

faq.q: Is Oaxaca good for couples?
faq.a: Yes — a slow, sensory, non-beach romance. Boutique casonas and the ex-convent (1576) Quinta Real, mezcal-tasting date nights, and the artisan-village shopping ritual (Teotitlán weaving, rugs $75–$500; San Bartolo black pottery; alebrijes) make the case.

faq.q: What makes Ometepe Island special?
faq.a: Ometepe is the largest island in a freshwater lake in the world and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2010, formed by two volcanoes — active Concepción (1,610 m) and dormant Maderas (1,394 m) — joined by the Isthmus of Istián across roughly 276 km². It also holds over 1,700 pre-Columbian petroglyphs across more than 100 documented sites.

faq.q: How hard are the Ometepe volcano hikes?
faq.a: Both are serious. Concepción is a strenuous ~10-hour dawn-start climb; Maderas is ~8 hours via a ~4.5 km trail from Balgüe / Finca Magdalena, with a crater lagoon you can swim in at the summit. A licensed local guide is mandatory for both because the upper slopes are exposed, muddy, and cloud-forest-slick.

faq.q: Where can you swim on Ometepe?
faq.a: Ojo de Agua ("eye of the water") is the island's signature spot — a natural mineral swimming hole fed by an underground river originating on Volcán Maderas, about 2 km from Santo Domingo. Go early or late to avoid crowds. Maderas' summit crater lagoon and designated lake beaches are the other locally advised swims.

faq.q: Where do couples stay on Ometepe?
faq.a: Ometepe skews to off-grid eco-lodges rather than resorts. Totoco Eco-Lodge (8 design cabins on Maderas' slopes, lake-and-Concepción views, farm-to-table dining), Finca del Sol (a 100% sustainable eco-lodge with permaculture farm), and Hacienda Mérida give the quiet, unscripted, two-people-and-a-volcano energy.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Two things: political detention and remoteness. Per the State Department, US nationals face serious risk of wrongful detention, exit bans, and detentions of weeks-plus, with some crimes carrying 50+ year sentences. And there is no trauma-grade care on-island — comprehensive care exists only in Managua, so a serious case realistically means Managua then a US medical evacuation.

faq.q: Is climbing an active volcano here dangerous?
faq.a: Concepción is an active stratovolcano (its last significant ash event was March 2010), and its summit hike is strenuous, exposed, and dawn-started; Maderas is dormant but steep, muddy, and cloud-forest-slick. A licensed guide is mandatory on both, and you should check volcanic status before going — though all of this fires as content only under the Level 3 advisory.

faq.q: Do you need a guide to hike Corcovado National Park?
faq.a: Yes — a certified guide is legally mandatory for all Corcovado entry, a SINAC rule in force since February 1, 2014 and enforced at every ranger station, where unguided visitors are turned away. Build the guided-trek product; there is no compliant self-guided version to sell.

faq.q: Can you dive Cocos Island on a day trip?
faq.a: No. Cocos is liveaboard-only — it lies ~342 mi off the Pacific coast, an ~36-hr open-ocean crossing from Puntarenas, and is sold as 8/10/12-night charters (15/21/27 dives) via Aggressor or Undersea Hunter. Berths book 6–18 months out, so plan far ahead.

faq.q: Are the Osa eco-lodges right for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — the Osa is honeymoon-grade seclusion without the resort cliché: private-reserve bungalows over the Pacific, canopy suites and no Wi-Fi. Lapa Rios alone offers 16 ocean-view bungalows across 1,000 protected acres, and remote lodges bundle meals, guided excursions and transfers by necessity.

faq.q: When can you see whales in Golfo Dulce?
faq.a: Golfo Dulce — one of only four tropical fjords on Earth — draws both hemispheres' humpbacks, so the season is unusually long: Southern-hemisphere humpbacks calve July–November (prime late Aug–Sept), and Northern-hemisphere humpbacks arrive November–February.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on a Corcovado trek?
faq.a: The tide-timed river crossings. Rio Sirena and Rio Claro are the most dangerous, with American crocodiles and bull sharks patrolling the river mouths, so guides cross only at low tide and never in storms. This — plus jungle heat and deep-remote medevac — is the true gatekeeper, above petty crime.

faq.q: Is diving Cocos Island dangerous?
faq.a: It is advanced diving in a strong-current, deeply remote environment. DAN membership and dive insurance are essential, no-fly-after-diving surface intervals apply, and because the site is ~36 hr from land the vessel itself is the only evacuation. Not a first-timer's trip.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for Palau, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Palau at Level 1 - Exercise Normal Precautions, and the UK FCDO issues no advice against travel, describing crime levels as low. Both note practical hazards rather than restrictions: unexploded WWII ordnance (found mainly on Peleliu - stay on marked paths and do not touch ordnance), diving hazards, and tropical cyclones, with an overnight curfew in Koror. The two governments agree on a Level 1 posture. Carry DAN membership plus dive-accident insurance with strong evacuation cover - the Palau Siren operator stresses that insurance covering emergency evacuation, chamber treatment and medical costs is a must - and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Palau has one hyperbaric facility for divers - a recompression chamber at Belau National Hospital in Koror. Hospital sources describe it as operational in 2026 with a trained barotrauma team, but availability can vary, so confirm its status with your dive operator or DAN before the trip. Because the archipelago is dispersed, serious cases can require evacuation by speedboat from the vessel and, in some cases, onward air evacuation to Manila - which is why evacuation-grade dive insurance matters here.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Palau, and when do the mantas aggregate?
faq.a: The peak liveaboard season is November through May, with warm water (28-30C) year-round. For mantas at German Channel, the winter months are best - January and February can bring dozens of mantas to the cleaning station.

faq.q: Which sites define a Palau liveaboard week?
faq.a: Blue Corner (the reef-hook shark drift), German Channel (mantas), Ulong Channel (a drift past giant clams and lettuce coral), the Blue Holes cavern, the Peleliu walls, Siaes Tunnel and New Drop-Off - plus the snorkel-only Jellyfish Lake as a non-dive highlight.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Blue Corner, Peleliu Express and the channel dives are strong-current drift dives where a reef hook and good buoyancy are essential, best suited to experienced divers; sheltered reefs, Chandelier Cave and the lake suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards for the multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the operator briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Palau liveaboards book?
faq.a: The November-May peak on the marquee vessels fills earliest, with the January-February manta weeks in most demand; hold roughly 6-12 months out for peak windows and preferred boats, nearer term for the shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for — is the road dangerous?
faq.a: The road is the risk, not the ruins. The overland San Cristóbal↔Palenque highway via Ocosingo (Chilón) has a documented armed-robbery history — one reported incident had ~18 men with assault rifles set a roadblock and rob a line of tourist vehicles, with the worst incidents after dark. The rule is daytime-only, guided/convoy transfer, no self-drive, and the safer, longer Villahermosa toll-road approach where possible.

faq.q: How remote is medical care from Palenque?
faq.a: Genuinely remote — plan for it. Palenque is a small town with limited advanced care; serious trauma routes to Villahermosa or Tuxtla Gutiérrez, with air evacuation to Mexico City for anything major. Bonampak, Yaxchilán and the deep-jungle waterfalls are hours from a hospital, so carry evacuation insurance — and note dengue is present year-round with malaria risk in rural Chiapas.

faq.q: What will I see at the Palenque ruins?
faq.a: A Maya city the rainforest never fully released: the Temple of the Inscriptions rising over Pakal the Great's tomb, and the four-story observation tower of the Palace, its civic heart. The tomb chamber itself has been closed to descent since ~2004 to protect it, so you see the pyramid and Pakal's regalia at the site museum, not the crypt. Go at the 8 AM opening before the jungle heat.

faq.q: What are the Palenque waterfalls, and when should I go?
faq.a: Three systems within reach: Agua Azul's 500+ turquoise cascades over ~6 km, the ~35 m Misol-Ha plunge with a walk-behind grotto, and the quieter Roberto Barrios falls with a natural rock slide (~45 min south, entry ~30 MXN). Come November–April, when the mineral-rich water runs brilliant turquoise; in the May–October rains sediment turns Agua Azul brown. Swim only in marked zones — currents are strong.

faq.q: Can I visit Bonampak and Yaxchilán?
faq.a: Yes, as a full-day guided expedition. Bonampak holds the best-preserved Classic Maya murals in existence (~792 AD), and Yaxchilán is reachable only by motorboat on the Usumacinta River, the water border with Guatemala. Go with a licensed operator, not an ad-hoc boatman, verify current border and security conditions before booking, and travel by daylight with life vests.
